PCG_AttribAdjust.summary: Builds or edits one numeric attribute through a fixed pipeline of initialize, adjustment stack, remap and post-process.
PCG_AttribAdjust.description:
A single-node alternative to Houdini's Attribute Adjust Float, Integer and Vector. Values are always handled as an array with one to four components, so one node covers all three; the component count is taken from the existing attribute, or from `size` when the attribute is created.

The four stages always run in the same order: **Initialize**, then the **Adjustments** stack, then **Remap**, then **Post-Process**. The order matters: Remap needs to see the final distribution to pick its automatic input range, and rounding must come last (rounding before a multiply by 2 would give even numbers). Only elements in `group` are processed, and the automatic remap range looks only at the elements in the group, so outliers outside the group cannot squash the contrast. Elements outside the group keep their original value.

The Adjustments parameter is a text stack with one step per line, because ComfyUI widgets cannot grow like a Houdini multiparm. Each line is `<operation> <source> [mask=<source>]`; text after `#` is a comment:

```
mul   2.0
add   @curvature
mul   rand(0.8, 1.2)
add   noise(perlin, 2.0, 0.3)
mix   1.0 mask=@occlusion
set   (@P.y * 0.1)
```

Operations are `set add sub mul div min max pow mix`. A source is a number, a comma-separated vector, `@attribute`, `rand(min, max)`, `noise(type, size, amplitude)`, or a wrangle expression in parentheses. A single value is spread over all components. `mask=` is per step and controls how much of that step is applied (0..1); for `mix` the mask is the interpolation factor itself (0.5 if omitted). `div` raises an error naming the line if any divisor is zero, and `pow` errors on negative bases with non-integer exponents instead of producing NaN.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the attribute written. Existing attribute types are kept (integer attributes are rounded).

params.group: Group pattern restricting which elements are adjusted. Elements outside the group keep their values.
params.attribute_class: Attribute class that holds the attribute.
params.attribute_name: Name of the attribute to edit or create. String attributes are rejected.
params.create_if_missing: Create the attribute when it does not exist. When off, a missing attribute is an error. A missing attribute also needs Initialize to be something other than Off, since there is no original value to keep.
params.size: Number of components of a newly created attribute (1 to 4). Ignored when the attribute already exists.
params.to_int: Create a new attribute as 32-bit integer instead of float. Has no effect on an existing attribute, which keeps its type.
params.initialize: Where the starting values come from. Off keeps the current values; Constant, Random, Noise and Expression generate new values; Attribute copies another attribute.
params.constant_x: Constant used by Initialize = Constant. Only as many components as the attribute has are used.
params.source_attribute: Attribute copied by Initialize = Attribute. A single-component source is spread over all components.
params.distribution: Distribution for Initialize = Random. Uniform fills Rand Min..Rand Max; Gaussian uses mean and standard deviation; Power raises the uniform value to the exponent before scaling to Rand Min..Rand Max.
params.rand_min: Lower end of the random range (Uniform and Power distributions).
params.rand_max: Upper end of the random range (Uniform and Power distributions).
params.gaussian_stddev: Standard deviation of the Gaussian distribution.
params.power_exponent: Exponent for the Power distribution. Values above 1 bias results toward Rand Min.
params.noise_size: Feature size of the noise in world units; the point position is divided by this value.
params.noise_amplitude: Multiplier applied to the noise value.
params.expression: Wrangle-style expression evaluated per element for Initialize = Expression, for example `@P.y`. A scalar result is spread over all components.
params.rand_seed: Seed for the random and noise sources, including `rand()` and `noise()` in the Adjustments stack.
params.id_attribute: Optional numeric attribute whose first component replaces the element number as the random key for Initialize = Random, so the random values follow an id instead of the element order.
params.adjustments: Adjustment stack, one step per line: `<operation> <source> [mask=<source>]`. See the node description for the syntax.
params.remap_ramp: Ramp applied after the value is normalized to 0..1. Written as `position:value` pairs separated by spaces.
params.input_range: Auto uses the minimum and maximum of the processed elements; Manual uses In Min and In Max.
params.in_min: Input value that maps to 0 in Manual input range. Values outside the range are clamped.
params.in_max: Input value that maps to 1 in Manual input range.
params.out_min: Output value that ramp value 0 maps to.
params.out_max: Output value that ramp value 1 maps to.
params.range_per_component: In Auto mode, find the range separately for each component. When off, all components share one range, which keeps a grey color grey when remapping `Cd`.
params.clamp_min: Lower limit applied per component when Use Clamp Min is on.
params.clamp_max: Upper limit applied per component when Use Clamp Max is on.
params.normalize: Unit Length scales each vector to length 1 (zero vectors stay zero); Sum To One divides by the component sum.
params.round_mode: Rounding applied last to every component.

PCG_AttribAdjust.houdini_notes: Combines Attribute Adjust Float, Integer and Vector in one node and uses its own Initialize / Adjustments / Remap / Post-Process model instead of Houdini's Operation and Pattern Type. For the Houdini-style behaviour use the dedicated Attribute Adjust Float, Integer, Vector and Color nodes.
tips: Because a missing attribute with Initialize = Off is an error, set Initialize to Constant when you only want to create an attribute.
Use `mask=` on a step to apply an operation only where an attribute (for example occlusion) is high.

PCG_AttribAdjustColor.summary: Generates or modifies a color attribute with constant, random, noise, attribute-driven or bounding-box patterns, then color-corrects and blends it.
PCG_AttribAdjustColor.description:
Follows the Houdini Attribute Adjust Color workflow. Stages in order: optional overwrite of the initial color, the **adjustment color** (from the pattern type) combined with the existing color by the operation, **color correction** (hue, saturation, value, brightness, gain, contrast, gamma, in that order), **post-process** (minimum, maximum, complement) and finally **blend** with the original input. Blend is last, so a blend of 0 really means no change, including the correction and post-process stages.

Random and Noise patterns use a separate random or noise value per RGB channel when interpolating between a min and max color. With a color ramp, a single value indexes the ramp. With Specific Colors, a single value picks one color from the list or scheme, weighted by `w=`. Noise values are not equalized, so they cluster around the middle of the range.

Elements outside `group` keep their original color. The attribute is created as a float color if it does not exist.

inputs.geo: Geometry whose color attribute is edited.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the color attribute written.

params.group: Group pattern restricting which elements are adjusted. Elements outside the group keep their values.
params.blend_mode: Whether the blend amount is a constant or read from an attribute.
params.blend: Blend amount between the original value (0) and the adjusted result (1).
params.blend_attribute: Numeric attribute (clamped to 0..1) giving the blend amount per element.
params.attribute_name: Name of the color attribute, which must have three numeric components. It is created if missing.
params.attribute_class: Attribute class that holds the attribute.
params.delete_other_colors: Remove attributes of the same name on the other classes. A point color would otherwise override a primitive color, so this makes the class you write to the one that shows.
params.overwrite_initial: Replace the starting color before the operation with the color chosen in Initial Color From.
params.initial_from: Source of the starting color: a constant, a 3-component color attribute, or a float attribute spread over RGB.
params.initial_color_r: Starting color for Initial Color From = Constant.
params.initial_attribute: Attribute read for the starting color when Initial Color From is an attribute.
params.adjust_value: Turns the adjustment off when disabled, so only the later stages (blend, clamp, and so on) are applied.
params.operation: How the adjustment color is combined with the existing color, per channel. Overlay branches on the existing color (below 0.5 multiplies, above screens); Screen is 1-(1-a)(1-b); Hard Mix gives 1 where the sum reaches 1 and 0 elsewhere; Difference is adjustment minus original, without absolute value. If the attribute does not exist yet, every operation writes the adjustment color.
params.pattern_type: How the adjustment color is generated. Constant uses one color; Random and Noise pick colors from the range settings; Color Attribute reads a color attribute; Remap Attribute maps a float attribute through the color ramp; Bounding Box maps position along a direction through the color ramp.
params.color_r: Adjustment color for Pattern Type = Constant.
params.range_values: Where Random and Noise colors come from: between a min and max color, along a color ramp, or from a specific list or color scheme.
params.color_space: Color space in which Min/Max interpolate. In HSV the three components are hue (0..1 is a full turn), saturation and value, and the result is converted back to RGB.
params.min_color_r: Color at the low end of Min/Max. Components are interpreted according to Color Space.
params.max_color_r: Color at the high end of Min/Max. Components are interpreted according to Color Space.
params.color_ramp: Color ramp as `position:r,g,b` entries separated by spaces. Used by Random/Noise with Color Ramp, and by Remap Attribute and Bounding Box.
params.color_scheme: Specific Colors source. Custom uses the color list; the other schemes derive colors from a base color in HSV: Constant (the base), Complementary (+180 degrees), Analogous 2 and 4 (neighbours spaced by Distance), Triadic (+-120 degrees), Tetradic, 5 Shades (value scaled by 1, .8, .6, .4, .2) and 5 Tints (saturation scaled the same way).
params.scheme_color_r: Base color the color scheme is derived from.
params.scheme_distance: Hue spacing in degrees for the Analogous and Tetradic schemes. Shades and Tints use a fixed step.
params.color_list: Colors for Specific Colors with the Custom scheme, one `r g b` per line. Append `w=weight` to set the probability of that color. Lines starting with `#` are comments.
params.adjustment_attribute: Color attribute (three components) read when Pattern Type = Color Attribute.
params.source_attribute: Float attribute (first component) mapped through the color ramp when Pattern Type = Remap Attribute.
params.bbox_direction_x: Direction along which position is projected for Pattern Type = Bounding Box. The vector is normalized, then the projected values are normalized to 0..1 and looked up in the color ramp.
params.compute_range: Take the minimum and maximum of the selected elements as the source range. When off, Source Min and Source Max are used.
params.source_min: Source range used when Compute Range is off (first value = minimum, second = maximum). Values outside it are clamped to the ends of the ramp.
params.randomization_by: Where the random seed key comes from: the element number, or the values of a custom attribute so the result follows the element rather than its index.
params.custom_attribute: Numeric attribute whose first component is used as the random key when Randomization By is Custom Attribute.
params.rand_seed: Seed for the Random and Noise patterns.
params.noise_type: Noise basis used when the pattern type is Noise. The `*_f2f1` variants return the difference between the second and first nearest feature distance.
params.location_attribute: Attribute that supplies the sample position for the noise. It is read from the target attribute class if it exists there as a 3-component attribute, otherwise it is taken from the point attribute of that name (vertices use their point, primitives their center, detail the mean position).
params.element_size: Feature size of the noise in world units. The sample position is divided by `element_size` multiplied by `element_scale`.
params.element_scale_x: Per-axis scale applied on top of `element_size`, so the noise can be stretched along one axis.
params.noise_offset_x: Offset added to the sample position before it is divided by the element size. Moves the noise pattern through space.
params.fractal_type: How octaves are combined. None gives a single octave; Standard sums octaves with falling weights; Terrain multiplies octaves so low areas flatten out; Hybrid Terrain is a multifractal with clamped weights.
params.max_octaves: Number of noise layers stacked when the fractal type is not None.
params.lacunarity: Frequency multiplier from one octave to the next.
params.roughness: Amplitude falloff from one octave to the next. Lower values give smoother results.
params.saturation: Multiplier for HSV saturation (result clamped to 0..1).
params.brightness: Amount added to HSV value after the Value multiplier.
params.gain: Multiplier applied to RGB after the HSV step.
params.minimum: Lower clamp, applied when Use Minimum is on.
params.maximum: Upper clamp, applied when Use Maximum is on.
params.complement: Invert the final color to `1 - color`.

PCG_AttribAdjustColor.houdini_notes: The Color Map pattern (texture sampling) and the viewport-handle Line / Radial gradients are not implemented, and the color-correction parameters have no per-attribute variant. Color Correction order, the Overlay and Screen formulas and the 5 Shades / 5 Tints steps are fixed choices of this plugin. The Color SOP equivalent is the separate Color node.
tips: Use Remap Attribute with a float attribute such as curvature to color geometry through a ramp.
Set Delete Other Colors when a point color is hiding the primitive color you just wrote.

PCG_AttribAdjustFloat.summary: Sets, offsets or scales a float attribute using constant, random, noise or attribute-driven values.
PCG_AttribAdjustFloat.description:
Follows the Houdini Attribute Adjust Float model. An **adjustment value** is generated by the Pattern Type (Constant, Random, Noise, Attribute) and merged into the existing value by the Operation. The result is blended with the original (constant or per-element amount) and optionally clamped with Minimum / Maximum. Elements outside `group` keep their value.

Random and Noise first produce a value `u` in 0..1 which Range Values maps to the final range. Random is uniform and keyed on the element number (or a custom attribute). Noise is the fractal noise mapped from -1..1 to 0..1; it is not equalized, so noise-driven values cluster in the middle of the range and rarely reach the ends. With Specific Values the same `u` selects from a weighted value list, so in Noise mode the discrete values appear in coherent patches.

If the attribute does not exist it is created as a float, and every operation (including Set Initial) just writes the adjustment value. A component suffix such as `v.x` edits one component; a vector attribute named without suffix gets its length adjusted.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the attribute written.

params.group: Group pattern restricting which elements are adjusted. Elements outside the group keep their values.
params.attribute_name: Attribute to edit. A component suffix such as `v.x` or `v[1]` edits only that component; a vector attribute without a suffix has its length adjusted (direction kept, zero vectors stay zero). The attribute is created if missing.
params.attribute_class: Attribute class that holds the attribute.
params.adjust_value: Turns the adjustment off when disabled, so only the later stages (blend, clamp, and so on) are applied.
params.operation: How the adjustment is combined with the existing value. Set Always overwrites; Set Initial only writes when the attribute did not exist; the others combine per element. If the attribute does not exist yet, every operation simply writes the adjustment value.
params.pattern_type: How the adjustment value is generated: a constant, a random value, a noise value or another attribute.
params.constant_value: Adjustment value for Pattern Type = Constant.
params.adjustment_attribute: Attribute read when the pattern type is Attribute.
params.attribute_adjustment: How the adjustment attribute is modified before use: scaled, offset, or both.
params.attribute_scale: Multiplier applied to the adjustment attribute.
params.attribute_offset: Value added to the adjustment attribute.
params.randomization_by: Where the random seed key comes from: the element number, or the values of a custom attribute so the result follows the element rather than its index.
params.custom_attribute: Numeric attribute whose first component is used as the random key when Randomization By is Custom Attribute.
params.rand_seed: Seed for the Random and Noise patterns.
params.minimum: Lower clamp, applied when Use Minimum is on.
params.maximum: Upper clamp, applied when Use Maximum is on.
params.range_values: How the random or noise value in 0..1 is mapped to a value. Min/Max interpolates between the two bounds; Min + Range Length goes from Min up by the length; Middle +- Range Length is centred on Middle with a total width equal to the length (half-width = length / 2); Specific Values picks from the value list.
params.min_value: Lower bound of the range (Min/Max and Min + Range Length modes).
params.max_value: Upper bound of the range (Min/Max mode).
params.middle_value: Centre of the range (Middle +- Range Length mode).
params.range_length: Length of the range. In Middle +- Range Length mode the half-width is half of this value.
params.value_list: Values to pick from when Range Values is Specific Values. One group per line: numbers separated by spaces, commas or semicolons, where `min-max:step` expands to a series. Append `w=weight` to a line to set the probability of that group; the values inside a group are chosen evenly. Lines starting with `#` are comments.
params.value_distribution: Shape of the distribution. Uniform maps the value directly; Uniform Remap passes it through the remap ramp first; Uniform with Outliers sends a percentage of elements outside the range.
params.remap_ramp: Ramp used by Uniform Remap. The horizontal axis is the random value (left = Min, right = Max), the vertical axis is the position inside the range.
params.outlier_percent: Percentage of elements that become outliers (Uniform with Outliers).
params.outlier_range: How far outliers extend beyond the range. In Additive mode it is an absolute distance; in Multiplicative mode the extension is (value - 1) times the range length.
params.outlier_range_mode: Additive extends the range by a fixed distance; Multiplicative extends it by a multiple of the range length.
params.outlier_extent: Which side outliers fall on: above the maximum, below the minimum, or either side at random.
params.outlier_seed: Seed for choosing which elements are outliers and how far they go.
params.outlier_attribute: Optional name of an integer attribute (same class) that receives 1 for outlier elements and 0 otherwise. Empty means no attribute is written.
params.use_stepping: Snap generated values to a grid of `step_size`, counted from the minimum of the range.
params.step_size: Grid spacing used when stepping is on.
params.noise_type: Noise basis used when the pattern type is Noise. The `*_f2f1` variants return the difference between the second and first nearest feature distance.
params.location_attribute: Attribute that supplies the sample position for the noise. It is read from the target attribute class if it exists there as a 3-component attribute, otherwise it is taken from the point attribute of that name (vertices use their point, primitives their center, detail the mean position).
params.element_size: Feature size of the noise in world units. The sample position is divided by `element_size` multiplied by `element_scale`.
params.element_scale_x: Per-axis scale applied on top of `element_size`, so the noise can be stretched along one axis.
params.noise_offset_x: Offset added to the sample position before it is divided by the element size. Moves the noise pattern through space.
params.fractal_type: How octaves are combined. None gives a single octave; Standard sums octaves with falling weights; Terrain multiplies octaves so low areas flatten out; Hybrid Terrain is a multifractal with clamped weights.
params.max_octaves: Number of noise layers stacked when the fractal type is not None.
params.lacunarity: Frequency multiplier from one octave to the next.
params.roughness: Amplitude falloff from one octave to the next. Lower values give smoother results.
params.blend_mode: Whether the blend amount is a constant or read from an attribute.
params.blend: Blend amount between the original value (0) and the adjusted result (1).
params.blend_attribute: Numeric attribute (clamped to 0..1) giving the blend amount per element.

PCG_AttribAdjustFloat.houdini_notes: Unit Settings, VEXpression, Animate Noise, Warping and Default Value are not implemented. Middle +- Range Length uses half the length on each side (as Attribute Adjust does; Attribute Noise defines the same mode with the full width). Houdini does not document whether noise is equalized; here it is not. The Specific Values list is written one group per line with the group's weight as the selection probability. Outlier extension in Multiplicative mode is measured in range lengths so that a range starting at 0 can still extend.
tips: Set Outlier Attribute to get a mask of the elements that were sent outside the range.

PCG_AttribAdjustVector.summary: Adjusts a vector attribute by direction and length, with constant, random, noise or attribute-driven values.
PCG_AttribAdjustVector.description:
Follows the Houdini Attribute Adjust Vector workflow: **Pre-Process** (optionally overwrite the starting vector, reverse it, normalize it, scale its length), the **adjustment** (per Adjustment For and Operation), then **Post-Process** (blend with the original, length scale, minimum and maximum length, unit length and an optional length attribute). Elements outside `group` keep their vector.

In Direction & Length mode the adjustment is a vector, produced by Adjust With: a constant, an attribute, or random / noise values drawn per component with independent random streams (so vectors are not confined to the diagonal). Direction Only and Length Only use a scalar adjustment (length, angle or bias) taken from the Float-style Range Values settings. Direction Only operations keep the original length; zero vectors stay zero for Direction Only and Length Only.

The outlier attribute, if named, is written as an integer 0/1 mask.

inputs.geo: Geometry whose vector attribute is adjusted.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the vector attribute written.

params.group: Group pattern restricting which elements are adjusted. Elements outside the group keep their values.
params.attribute_name: Name of a 3-component numeric attribute. Created as a float vector if missing.
params.attribute_class: Attribute class that holds the attribute.
params.enable_preprocess: Enables the Pre-Process options (overwrite initial value, reverse, unit length, length scale).
params.overwrite_initial: Replace the starting vector with the one chosen in Initial Value From before the adjustment.
params.initial_from: Source of the starting vector: a constant, the computed normal of the chosen class, or another attribute.
params.initial_vector_x: Starting vector for Initial Value From = Constant.
params.initial_attribute: Attribute read for the starting vector. A single-component attribute is spread over all three components.
params.pre_unit_length: Normalize the starting vector to length 1 (zero vectors stay zero).
params.pre_length_scale: Factor the starting vector is multiplied by when Use Pre Length Scale is on.
params.adjust_value: Turns the adjustment off when disabled, so only the later stages (blend, clamp, and so on) are applied.
params.adjustment_for: What the adjustment changes. Direction & Length edits the whole vector with a vector adjustment value; Direction Only changes the direction and keeps the length; Length Only changes the length and keeps the direction (scalar adjustment value).
params.operation: How the adjustment is combined. Allowed operations depend on Adjustment For, and an invalid combination is an error: Direction & Length allows Set Always, Set Initial, Set, Add, Subtract, Multiply, Minimum, Maximum; Direction Only allows Add, Subtract (the result is renormalized to the original length), Rotate (about the axis by an angle), Spread (onto a cone around the original direction, random azimuth) and Interpolate (spherically toward the goal); Length Only allows Add, Subtract, Multiply, Minimum, Maximum.
params.adjust_with: How the adjustment value is generated: constant, random, noise, or from an attribute.
params.constant_vector_x: Adjustment vector for Adjust With = Constant when the adjustment is a vector.
params.scalar_value: Adjustment value for Adjust With = Constant when the adjustment is a scalar: the length change for Length Only, the angle in degrees for Rotate and Spread, and the Bias (0..1) for Interpolate.
params.vector_range: Range used for random and noise vectors. Positive spans 0..Amplitude; Zero Centered spans -0.5..0.5 times Amplitude (so amplitude 1 gives +-0.5); Min/Max interpolates between two vectors; Specific Values picks from the vector list.
params.amplitude: Overall size of Positive and Zero Centered vector ranges.
params.min_vector_x: Lower corner of the Min/Max vector range.
params.max_vector_x: Upper corner of the Min/Max vector range.
params.vector_list: Vectors for Specific Values, one `x y z` per line. Append `w=weight` to set the probability of that vector. Lines starting with `#` are comments.
params.range_values: Range mapping used for scalar random and noise adjustments (length change, angle, bias). See the Float node: Min/Max, Min + Range Length, Middle +- Range Length (half-width = length / 2) or Specific Values.
params.min_value: Lower bound of the range (Min/Max and Min + Range Length modes).
params.max_value: Upper bound of the range (Min/Max mode).
params.middle_value: Centre of the range (Middle +- Range Length mode).
params.range_length: Length of the range. In Middle +- Range Length mode the half-width is half of this value.
params.value_list: Values for scalar adjustments when Range Values is Specific Values. One group per line: numbers separated by spaces, commas or semicolons, where `min-max:step` expands to a series; append `w=weight` for the group's probability. Not to be confused with the vector list.
params.value_distribution: Shape of the distribution. Uniform maps the value directly; Uniform Remap passes it through the remap ramp first; Uniform with Outliers sends a percentage of elements outside the range.
params.remap_ramp: Ramp used by Uniform Remap. The horizontal axis is the random value (left = Min, right = Max), the vertical axis is the position inside the range.
params.outlier_percent: Percentage of elements that become outliers (Uniform with Outliers).
params.outlier_range: How far outliers extend beyond the range. In Additive mode it is an absolute distance; in Multiplicative mode the extension is (value - 1) times the range length.
params.outlier_range_mode: Additive extends the range by a fixed distance; Multiplicative extends it by a multiple of the range length.
params.outlier_extent: Which side outliers fall on: above the maximum, below the minimum, or either side at random.
params.outlier_seed: Seed for choosing which elements are outliers and how far they go.
params.outlier_attribute: Optional name of an integer attribute (same class) that receives 1 for outlier elements and 0 otherwise. Empty means no attribute is written.
params.use_stepping: Snap generated values to a grid of `step_size`, counted from the minimum of the range.
params.step_size: Grid spacing used when stepping is on.
params.axis_from: Whether the Rotate axis is a constant or read from an attribute.
params.axis_attribute: Vector attribute giving the rotation axis per element.
params.goal_from: Whether the Interpolate goal direction is a constant or read from an attribute.
params.goal_attribute: Vector attribute giving the goal direction per element.
params.adjustment_attribute: Attribute read when Adjust With = Attribute. For vector adjustments it needs three components (or one, spread over all three); for scalar adjustments the first component is used.
params.randomization_by: Where the random seed key comes from: the element number, or the values of a custom attribute so the result follows the element rather than its index.
params.custom_attribute: Numeric attribute whose first component is used as the random key when Randomization By is Custom Attribute.
params.rand_seed: Seed for Random and Noise adjustments. It also determines the azimuth used by Spread.
params.blend_mode: Whether the blend amount is a constant or read from an attribute.
params.blend: Blend amount between the original value (0) and the adjusted result (1).
params.blend_attribute: Numeric attribute (clamped to 0..1) giving the blend amount per element.
params.blend_type: Linear blends the vectors component by component. Spherical interpolates the direction on the sphere and the length linearly.
params.post_length_scale: Factor the result is multiplied by when Use Post Length Scale is on.
params.min_length: Smallest allowed vector length when Use Min Length is on. Zero vectors have no direction and stay zero.
params.max_length: Largest allowed vector length when Use Max Length is on.
params.post_unit_length: Normalize the final vector to length 1 (zero vectors stay zero).
params.length_attribute: Optional name of a float attribute (same class) that receives the length of the final vector. Empty means nothing is written.
params.noise_type: Noise basis used when the pattern type is Noise. The `*_f2f1` variants return the difference between the second and first nearest feature distance.
params.location_attribute: Attribute that supplies the sample position for the noise. It is read from the target attribute class if it exists there as a 3-component attribute, otherwise it is taken from the point attribute of that name (vertices use their point, primitives their center, detail the mean position).
params.element_size: Feature size of the noise in world units. The sample position is divided by `element_size` multiplied by `element_scale`.
params.element_scale_x: Per-axis scale applied on top of `element_size`, so the noise can be stretched along one axis.
params.noise_offset_x: Offset added to the sample position before it is divided by the element size. Moves the noise pattern through space.
params.fractal_type: How octaves are combined. None gives a single octave; Standard sums octaves with falling weights; Terrain multiplies octaves so low areas flatten out; Hybrid Terrain is a multifractal with clamped weights.
params.max_octaves: Number of noise layers stacked when the fractal type is not None.
params.lacunarity: Frequency multiplier from one octave to the next.
params.roughness: Amplitude falloff from one octave to the next. Lower values give smoother results.

PCG_AttribAdjustVector.houdini_notes: Zero Centered vectors follow the Houdini documentation: values are shifted to -0.5..0.5 and then multiplied by Amplitude. The azimuth for Spread, and the formulas of Spherical blend, are this plugin's choices where Houdini does not specify them. Selecting an operation that does not match Adjustment For is an error rather than a silent substitution.

PCG_AttribBlur.summary: Smooths point or primitive attributes by diffusing them along mesh connectivity.
PCG_AttribBlur.description:
Not a spatial blur: values spread along edges (points) or across shared edges (primitives), so two pieces of geometry that are not connected never influence each other, however close they are. Typical uses are feathering scatter density maps, softening masks and turning hard `Connectivity` blocks into gradients.

Each iteration does `v += step * mask * (neighbour_average - v)`, an explicit heat diffusion. `step` is clamped to 0..1 because larger values oscillate and diverge; for a wider blur add iterations rather than increasing the step. There is deliberately no radius parameter: on a mesh with uneven edge lengths the same radius would be one step in sparse areas and ten in dense ones. The spread is roughly proportional to the square root of `iterations * step` edge lengths.

Elements outside `group`, or with a zero mask, are frozen (not written) but still contribute to their neighbours' averages, so the border of a blurred region is not held back by its own value. String attributes are skipped.

inputs.geo: Geometry with connectivity and the attributes to blur.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the blurred attributes written back with their original types (integer attributes are rounded).

params.group: Group pattern restricting which elements are modified. Others stay unchanged but still feed the averages.
params.attribute_class: Point diffuses along edges; Primitive diffuses between faces that share an edge. Vertex and detail attributes have no neighbourhood and are not supported.
params.attributes: Attribute names to blur, space separated, wildcards allowed (for example `uv*` or `* ^P`). Only numeric attributes are blurred. It is an error if nothing matches.
params.mode: Uniform averages the neighbours equally. Edge Length weights each neighbour by the inverse of its distance (points only), so closer neighbours count more.
params.iterations: Number of diffusion passes. More iterations spread values further.
params.step: Fraction of the way each element moves toward its neighbour average per pass. Clamped to 0..1.
params.mask_attribute: Optional numeric attribute (clamped to 0..1) that scales the step per element. 0 leaves the element fixed, though its value still influences neighbours.
params.invert_mask: Use `1 - mask` instead of the mask.

tips: Add iterations, not step, for a softer result.
Blur a mask attribute before using it as a scatter density to avoid hard edges.

PCG_AttribCast.summary: Changes the storage type of attributes between 32/64-bit float, 32/64-bit integer and string.
PCG_AttribCast.description:
Converts the data type of every attribute matching the name pattern in the chosen class. float64 gives more precision at twice the memory, int32 halves it, and string attributes are handy for tagging. Float to integer **rounds to the nearest integer** rather than truncating (2.9 becomes 3), because truncation tends to look like an upstream error.

Converting to string writes the components of each element as a space-separated text. Converting a string attribute to a number parses the text and errors out on values that cannot be read as numbers. Strings are left alone when the target is also string.

inputs.geo: Geometry with the attributes to convert.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the converted attributes.

params.attribute_class: Attribute class to look in.
params.attributes: Attribute names to convert, space separated, wildcards allowed (`*` means all). It is an error if nothing matches.
params.to_type: Target storage type. Integer targets round to the nearest value.

PCG_AttribComposite.summary: Composites a foreground attribute over a background attribute with a blend mode and alpha.
PCG_AttribComposite.description:
Blends attribute B (foreground) into attribute A (background) like image layers. The result is `A + alpha * (blend(A, B) - A)`, where `alpha` is the Alpha value multiplied by an optional per-element alpha attribute read from the foreground. The background comes from `geo`; the foreground comes from the `fg` input, or from `geo` itself when `fg` is not connected.

Foreground elements are paired with background elements by element number, or by the value of a match attribute (typically `id`; the first foreground element with that value is used). Background elements without a partner are left unchanged. Blend modes: over (take B), add, subtract, multiply, divide (A is kept where B is 0), screen, overlay (decided by A: below 0.5 multiplies, above screens), min, max, difference (absolute), average.

A single-component attribute is spread over the components of the other side. String attributes only support Over, in which case the foreground value is taken where alpha exceeds 0.5. The `report` output lists how many elements matched.

inputs.geo: Geometry that provides the background attribute and receives the result.
inputs.fg: Optional geometry that provides the foreground attribute. If not connected, the foreground is read from `geo` itself.

outputs.geo: Copy of `geo` with the composited attribute written.
outputs.report: Text summary with the numbers of matched and unmatched elements.

params.attribute_class: Attribute class of the background, foreground and result.
params.bg_attribute: Background attribute in `geo`. If it does not exist it is treated as zero.
params.fg_attribute: Foreground attribute, read from `fg` (or from `geo` when `fg` is not connected). It must exist.
params.mode: Blend function applied between background and foreground, per component.
params.alpha: Global opacity of the foreground, 0 to 1.
params.alpha_attribute: Optional numeric attribute on the foreground that multiplies Alpha per element. Unmatched elements get alpha 0.
params.match: How foreground elements are paired with background elements: by element number or by a matching attribute.
params.match_attribute: Attribute present on both sides whose values are compared when Match is By Attribute.
params.output: Name of the attribute to write. Empty writes back into the background attribute.

PCG_AttribComposite.houdini_notes: Foreground and background are attributes of geometry rather than image layers; the blend formulas are the common layer-blend equations.

PCG_AttribCopy.summary: Copies attributes and groups from a source geometry to a destination, element by element.
PCG_AttribCopy.description:
Moves attributes from `source` onto `dest` by **element number**, one to one. It is meant for the case where both sides were originally the same geometry (two branches that each computed something and are merged back). If topology has changed so numbers no longer line up, either match by an id attribute or use Attribute Transfer to look up by distance.

Elements whose number is beyond the source range keep their current value instead of being zero-filled; zero-filling would make an element-count mismatch look like a region of genuine zeros. With a match attribute, destination elements take the value from the first source element with the same value; those without a match are left alone. Groups listed in `groups` are copied with the same pairing.

inputs.source: Geometry the attributes are read from.

outputs.geo: Copy of `dest` with the copied attributes and groups.

params.group: Group pattern on `dest` limiting which elements are written.
params.attribute_class: Attribute class to copy within.
params.attributes: Names of source attributes to copy, space separated, wildcards allowed. It is an error if neither attributes nor groups match.
params.groups: Names of source groups of this class to copy, wildcards allowed. They are paired the same way as the attributes.
params.match_attribute: Attribute present on both geometries whose values pair the elements (typically `id`). Used only when Use Match Attribute is on.
params.use_match_attribute: Pair elements by Match Attribute instead of by element number.

PCG_AttribCopy.houdini_notes: Covers Attribute Copy and Group Copy together (the `groups` field).

PCG_AttribCreate.summary: Creates attributes and writes a constant or expression value, optionally only on a group.
PCG_AttribCreate.description:
Creates one or more attributes (names separated by spaces) of the chosen class and type and fills them with a value. If `group` is set, only the selected elements are written and the rest keep their existing value, or zero for a new attribute. This is the usual way to tag a subset of elements.

With Use Expression on, the value comes from a one-line wrangle expression evaluated per element (for example `@P.y` or `@ptnum % 3`) instead of the constant. The node exists to make the graph self-documenting: a named node reads better than another anonymous wrangle.

Types: Float and Integer use `size` components; Vector has 3 and Vector4 has 4; String writes `string_value`. Integer values are rounded. An existing attribute of a different component count is replaced.

inputs.geo: Geometry to add the attributes to.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the new or updated attributes.

params.group: Group pattern restricting which elements are written.
params.name: Attribute name(s) to create, separated by spaces. Each one gets the same value.
params.attribute_class: Class that the attribute is created on.
params.attribute_type: Data type. Vector is three components, Vector4 four; Float and Integer use Size.
params.size: Number of components for Float and Integer attributes.
params.value_x: Constant value. Only the first Size components (3 for Vector, 4 for Vector4) are used.
params.string_value: Text written when the type is String.
params.expression: Wrangle-style expression evaluated per element when Use Expression is on.
params.use_expression: Use the expression instead of the constant value.
params.only_if_missing: Skip names that already exist on the geometry instead of overwriting them.

PCG_AttribDelete.summary: Deletes attributes by name pattern on each attribute class, or keeps only the matching ones.
PCG_AttribDelete.description: Each class has its own name pattern field. Patterns accept wildcards (`uv*` matches everything starting with `uv`) and exclusions (`* ^P ^N` means all but `P` and `N`). An **empty field leaves that class untouched**, which matters especially with Delete Non Selected: an empty field is not interpreted as select-all. The point position `P` is never deleted, since geometry without positions is invalid.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input without the deleted attributes.

params.point: Point attribute names to delete, space separated, wildcards allowed. Empty leaves point attributes alone.
params.vertex: Vertex attribute names to delete. Empty leaves vertex attributes alone.
params.prim: Primitive attribute names to delete. Empty leaves primitive attributes alone.
params.detail: Detail attribute names to delete. Empty leaves detail attributes alone.
params.delete_non_selected: Delete everything that does not match instead. Classes with an empty field are still left alone.

PCG_AttribFade.summary: Writes a spatial falloff attribute that is full inside a group and fades out with distance from it.
PCG_AttribFade.description:
Starting from `group`, each element receives a value based on how far it is from the group. Elements inside the group get Inside Value; elements farther than `radius` get Outside Value; in between, the distance `d` is converted to `1 - d / radius`, shaped by the falloff ramp, and interpolated between Outside and Inside Value. Distance is measured either in edge steps or in world units along the surface, depending on Metric.

The usual use is a mask for Transform, Attribute Adjust or Noise ("lift only this area, with a smooth edge"). The ramp defaults to Smooth rather than Linear because a linear ramp has a slope discontinuity at the group border that shows up as a visible ridge when displaced.

With From Boundary on, the falloff runs on the inside of the group instead: the ring of elements touching the boundary is 0 and values rise toward 1 in the interior (full value beyond `radius` from the boundary); everything outside the group is 0. That produces a soft selection that is only full in the centre.

The group must select at least one element, otherwise the node errors (an empty group is treated as the empty set, not as all elements).

inputs.geo: Geometry to write the fade attribute on.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the fade attribute written.

params.group: Group pattern the fade starts from. It must select at least one element.
params.cls: Attribute class that the fade is computed and stored on (points or primitives). Distance on primitives is measured across shared edges.
params.attribute_name: Name of the output attribute. If it already exists as a single-component attribute it keeps its type and is combined according to Combine.
params.metric: Steps counts edge hops from the group; Distance measures world-space distance along the mesh.
params.radius: Fade length: number of steps or world distance (according to Metric) over which the value falls from inside to outside.
params.from_boundary: Fade toward the boundary from within the group instead of outward from it, giving a soft selection that is full only in the middle.
params.falloff_ramp: Ramp that shapes the falloff. The horizontal axis is `1 - d / radius` (0 at the far edge, 1 at the group), the vertical axis is the result before Inside / Outside scaling. Written as `position:value` pairs.
params.ramp_mode: Interpolation between ramp points. Smooth avoids the visible crease that Linear leaves at the group border.
params.inside_value: Value at the full end of the ramp (inside the group).
params.outside_value: Value at the far end of the ramp (beyond the radius).
params.invert: Invert the ramp result (`1 - v`) before applying Inside and Outside Value.
params.combine: How the new fade merges with an existing attribute of the same name: Set replaces it; Add, Multiply, Max and Min combine per element. A missing attribute counts as 0 (1 for Multiply).

tips: Plug the fade attribute into a mask-aware node such as Attribute Adjust or Transform to get smooth localized edits.

PCG_AttribFadeTime.summary: Fades a point attribute in, holds it, and fades it out over time using per-point start frames.
PCG_AttribFadeTime.description:
Time-based fade, following the Houdini Attribute Fade SOP. For each point the local time is `t = Frame - start`, where `start = start_attribute * start_retime + frame_offset` (0 if the start attribute is missing). Then:

- `0 <= t < fade_in`: fading in, evaluated through the Fade In Ramp at `t / fade_in`.
- `fade_in <= t < fade_in + hold`: fully on (1), where `hold = fade_hold * holdscale` (scale is 1 if the attribute is missing).
- Next `fade_out` frames: fading out through the Fade Out Ramp.
- Before the start or after the end: 0.

The result is `original * fade`; if the attribute does not exist it is created from 1, so it holds the fade itself. Only points in `group` are changed; others keep their value (or 1 for a newly created attribute). Phases with zero length are skipped.

The second and third inputs can supply the start frame and the hold scale instead of reading them from `geo`; they are matched by point number, so the point counts must be equal. The `report` output counts points at zero, fully on and mid-fade.

inputs.start_geo: Optional geometry to read the start frame attribute from (matched by point number, same point count as `geo`).
inputs.hold_geo: Optional geometry to read the hold scale attribute from (matched by point number, same point count as `geo`).

outputs.geo: Copy of `geo` with the faded attribute.
outputs.report: Text summary of how many points are at zero, fully on and fading.

params.visualize: Also write the fade value into `Cd` of the points in the group, for a quick look at the result.
params.group: Point group pattern limiting which points are faded.
params.fade_attribute: Point attribute that is multiplied by the fade. If it does not exist, it is created with the fade value itself.
params.start_attribute: Point attribute holding each point's start frame (from `start_geo` if connected). A missing attribute means start 0.
params.start_retime: Multiplier from the start attribute value to frames. Use the frame rate if the attribute stores seconds.
params.hold_scale_attribute: Point attribute that multiplies the hold duration per point (from `hold_geo` if connected). A missing attribute means 1.
params.frame: Current frame. ComfyUI has no global timeline, so drive this from a playbar or value node.
params.frame_offset: Frames added to every start frame.
params.fade_in: Duration of the fade-in, in frames.
params.fade_hold: Duration of the fully-on phase, in frames, before being scaled by the hold scale attribute.
params.fade_out: Duration of the fade-out, in frames.
params.fade_in_ramp: Curve for the fade-in. Horizontal axis is progress through the fade-in, vertical axis is the fade value. Written as `position:value` pairs.
params.fade_out_ramp: Curve for the fade-out. Horizontal axis is progress through the fade-out, vertical axis is the fade value (the default goes from 1 down to 0).

PCG_AttribFadeTime.houdini_notes: The current frame is an explicit parameter instead of the global time. Both ramps hold the actual fade value (fade-out is not reversed internally). Start Frame Retime is a single multiplier rather than a from/to pair. Spatial falloff from a group is the separate Attribute Fade node.

PCG_AttribFill.summary: Fills a point attribute from known points to the remaining points along mesh connectivity.
PCG_AttribFill.description:
The attribute is meaningful only on the *known* points (the `known_group`; if empty, the points whose attribute is not all zero). Values are propagated to the other points through the mesh edges, so disconnected pieces never exchange values. Points not connected to any known point keep their value (Poisson writes 0 there, Eikonal writes Unreachable Time).

Methods:

- **Harmonic** solves a Laplace equation with the known values as boundary conditions (conjugate gradient). The result is smooth and has no overshoot; extremes occur only on known points.
- **Nearest** copies the value of the closest known point measured along edges.
- **Diffuse** runs `iterations` of weighted averaging with the known points pinned. Few iterations give a soft transition near the known points; many converge to Harmonic.
- **Eikonal** writes the travel time along edges from the Boundary Group (`edge length / speed at the departing point`). It does not read the input values and requires a group. It follows edges, it is not a fast-marching solver.
- **Poisson** is a harmonic fill with edge weights `1 / edge length`, optionally guided by the gradient of Attribute to Match.
- **Diffusion** performs one implicit diffusion step from the current values; known points act as fixed sources. Without a group nothing is fixed. Repeat the node for more steps.
- **Extrapolate** copies values outward from the known points along shortest paths, either as plain scalars or, for vectors, by parallel transport of the tangential part.

The `report` output lists how many points were known, filled and unreachable.

inputs.geo: Geometry with a point attribute to fill.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the filled point attribute.
outputs.report: Text summary with the numbers of known, filled and unreachable points.

params.method: Fill algorithm; see the node description. Harmonic, Nearest and Diffuse use Weights and Iterations as applicable; the last four options correspond to Houdini's modes and use the parameters below.
params.attribute: Point attribute to fill. It must exist and be numeric, except for Eikonal which creates it.
params.speed_attribute: Optional point attribute giving the propagation speed for Eikonal and Diffusion. Values are limited below by Minimum Speed.
params.match_attribute: Optional attribute for Poisson whose differences between neighbours guide the fill (Attribute to Match).
params.weight_attribute: Optional point attribute (0..1) that controls how strongly Attribute to Match guides the Poisson fill.
params.known_group: Point group of known points (Boundary Group for the Houdini-style methods). Empty uses the points where the attribute is not all zero; Eikonal requires a group, Diffusion treats empty as no fixed sources.
params.weights: Edge weighting for Harmonic and Diffuse: Uniform gives every edge weight 1, Inverse Length gives shorter edges more weight.
params.iterations: Number of averaging passes for Diffuse.
params.min_edge_length: Lower limit on edge length used in the Poisson and Diffusion weights, to avoid division by tiny lengths.
params.min_speed: Lower limit on speed for Eikonal and Diffusion.
params.diffusion_time: Time step of the implicit Diffusion step. Larger values spread further.
params.unreachable_time: Value written by Eikonal on points that cannot be reached from the group.
params.extrapolation: Extrapolate behaviour. Scalar copies the value from the source point; Parallel Transport carries the tangent part of a vector attribute along the surface (needs 3 components, uses `N` or computed normals).
params.tangential_only: For Parallel Transport, write only the tangential part; when off, the normal component is copied from the source as in Scalar mode.
params.global_rotation: Extra rotation in degrees about the normal, applied to the transported tangent vectors.

PCG_AttribFill.houdini_notes: Harmonic, Nearest and Diffuse are this plugin's methods; Eikonal, Poisson, Diffusion and Extrapolate correspond to Houdini's modes. Eikonal travels along mesh edges, so the result is edge-path distance rather than a surface-accurate fast-marching time. Where Houdini does not specify the guide strength on edges for Poisson, the average of the two endpoint weights is used.

PCG_AttribFromMap.summary: Samples an image layer at the UVs of each element and writes the result as an attribute.
PCG_AttribFromMap.description:
The main way to bring an image (for example a mask or color map generated by a diffusion model) back onto geometry. The image comes from a COP network, the UVs from a `uv` attribute on the geometry.

UVs live on vertices, so writing to points is ambiguous at UV seams, where one point has several UVs. The class decides what happens: **Vertex** uses the vertex UV directly (recommended, no ambiguity); **Point** uses the UV of the first incident vertex (not an average, since averaging u=0 and u=1 at a seam would sample the middle of the image); **Primitive** averages the UVs of all its vertices. The `info` output reports how many points lie on seams.

Bilinear sampling reconstructs the image exactly in the interior; the half-pixel at the borders is governed by the border mode. Remember to use sRGB to Linear when treating the image as numeric data.

inputs.geo: Geometry with UVs that receives the attribute.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the sampled attribute.
outputs.info: Text summary: element count, component count, and the number of points on UV seams.

params.group: Group pattern limiting which elements are written. Others keep their current value (zero for a new attribute).
params.layer: Name of the image layer to sample, such as `C` for color.
params.name: Name of the attribute written. New attributes are created as floats.
params.channels: Channels to keep: empty for all, or a comma-separated list of channel indices such as `0` or `0,2`.
params.decode: Color transform applied to the sampled values. Use sRGB to Linear when the image is used as a number (displacement, density, `pscale`), since an encoded 0.5 is only about 0.214 in linear terms.
params.filter: Bilinear interpolates between pixels; Closest takes the nearest pixel.
params.border: Behaviour outside the image: Clamp repeats the edge pixels, Wrap tiles the image, Black returns zero.
params.scale: Multiplier applied to the sampled values (after decode).
params.blend: Mix between the existing attribute value (0) and the sampled value (1). A missing attribute counts as 0, and component counts are broadcast to match.
params.class: Attribute class that is written, which also selects how UVs are fetched. Vertex is the safest because UVs are stored on vertices.
params.uv_from: Where to read the UV attribute: Auto prefers the vertex attribute and falls back to the point attribute.
params.uv_scale_u: Multiplier on u and v before sampling, for tiling the image. The second value scales v.
params.uv_offset_u: Offset added to u and v after scaling. The second value offsets v.

PCG_AttribFromMap.houdini_notes: Also covers sampling an image layer in a COP network (Attribute from Layer, Geometry Attribute from Layer) since the image is taken from a COP input. UV scale and offset are built in so a texture can be tiled without a separate UV Transform.

PCG_AttribFromCamera.summary: Projects an image onto geometry through a camera, with visibility testing, and writes an attribute plus visible and mask groups.
PCG_AttribFromCamera.description:
Samples an image layer at the screen position of each element as seen by the camera. It does not need UVs, which makes it suitable for freshly imported meshes. A typical use is turning an AI-generated mask into a group: render a pass, feed it to a diffusion model, project the result back, and use `mask_group` to drive Blast, Fracture, PolyExtrude or Scatter, so the AI only decides *where* and the rest of the graph stays deterministic.

Plain camera projection ignores occlusion, so the back of a sphere would get the same color as the front. This node has four visibility levels: **All** (no test), **Frustum** (inside the image and in front of the camera), **Front** (adds a facing test against `normal_attrib`), and **Full** (adds occlusion, the default). Occlusion rasterizes the *whole* geometry from the camera, so objects outside `group` still hide others; `group` only limits what is written. Occlusion passes when the triangle visible at the element's pixel (searched in a 3x3 pixel neighbourhood) contains the element, or when its depth is within the bias of the visible depth.

Two groups are the point of the node: `visible_group` holds the elements the camera can see (for coverage checks across several cameras), `mask_group` holds visible elements whose written value reaches `threshold`. The test uses the value after scale and offset.

Elements that are not visible are handled by Missing: keep the old value (what multi-camera accumulation needs), write zero, or write a fixed value. The three extra outputs report the visible count, the coverage fraction and a text summary of the elements rejected (outside the frame, back-facing, occluded).

inputs.geo: Geometry to project onto and write attributes on.
inputs.cam: Camera used for the projection and for the visibility test.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the sampled attribute and the optional groups and UV attribute.
outputs.visible: Number of elements the camera sees (and that are in `group`).
outputs.coverage: Visible elements as a fraction of all elements of the class.
outputs.info: Text summary: visible/total, and counts of elements outside the frame, back-facing and occluded.

params.layer: Name of the image layer to sample, such as `C` for color.
params.name: Name of the attribute written. New attributes are created as floats.
params.channels: Channels to keep: empty for all, or a comma-separated list of channel indices such as `0` or `0,2`.
params.decode: Color transform applied to the sampled values. Use sRGB to Linear when the image is used as a number (displacement, density, `pscale`), since an encoded 0.5 is only about 0.214 in linear terms.
params.filter: Bilinear interpolates between pixels; Closest takes the nearest pixel.
params.border: Behaviour outside the image: Clamp repeats the edge pixels, Wrap tiles the image, Black returns zero.
params.scale: Multiplier applied to the sampled values (after decode).
params.blend: Mix between the existing attribute value (0) and the sampled value (1). A missing attribute counts as 0, and component counts are broadcast to match.
params.group: Group pattern limiting which elements are written. Occlusion still uses all geometry. Unselected elements count as not written for the groups.
params.class: Attribute class that is projected onto. Points and vertices use the point position; primitives use their center, so a large face can switch visibility as a whole at occlusion edges.
params.visibility: How strict the visibility test is: All (no test), Frustum (in frame and in front of the camera), Front (plus facing), Full (plus occlusion).
params.occlusion: Criterion for Full visibility. Element + Depth accepts an element if its own triangle is visible at its pixel or its depth matches; Element uses only the triangle test; Depth uses only the depth comparison, which misjudges grazing angles.
params.facing_min: Minimum cosine between the normal and the direction to the camera for Front and Full. The default 0.1 rejects grazing angles, where sampling is unreliable anyway. Elements without a normal are not tested.
params.depth_bias: Depth tolerance for the occlusion test, as a fraction of the bounding-sphere radius of the geometry, so it behaves the same for any model scale.
params.silhouette_guard: Number of pixels to erode the rasterized silhouette by before testing occlusion. Removes unreliable elements at the very edge of the shape. 0 disables the guard.
params.border_margin: Fraction of the image width and height at the border that counts as outside the frame.
params.normal_attrib: Normal attribute used for the facing test; computed on the fly when missing.
params.missing: What to write on elements that are not visible: Keep Original leaves the previous value (zero for a new attribute), Zero writes 0, Value writes the Missing Value.
params.missing_value: Value written on invisible elements when Missing is Value.
params.visible_group: Name of a group to create with the visible elements. Empty means no group.
params.mask_group: Name of a group to create with the visible elements whose attribute value is at least `threshold`. Empty means no group.
params.threshold: Threshold on the written value for `mask_group` (after scale, offset and blend).
params.threshold_channel: Component of the written attribute that is tested against the threshold. It must exist.
params.uv_name: If not empty, also write the projected screen UV (0..1) of every element into an attribute of this name.

PCG_AttribFromCamera.houdini_notes: Corresponds to a Position Sample in a COP network combined with a camera projection, with visibility, occlusion and group creation built in.
tips: Use visibility Full with Missing = Keep Original to accumulate paint from several cameras without the second pass erasing the first.
The depth bias is relative to model size, so imported meshes of any scale work with the default.

PCG_AttribFromPieces.summary: Assigns each element or piece a variant from a weighted library and writes it as an attribute.
PCG_AttribFromPieces.description:
Chooses a **variant** for every element (or for every piece, when a piece attribute is given) and writes it to `output`. Connected to Copy to Points as its piece attribute, it gives "several rocks scattered by weight".

Variants come from the `library` input: each distinct value of `library_attribute` is one variant (in order of first appearance), weighted by `weight_attribute`. Without a library, the variants are the integers 0 to Count-1 and the weights are typed into Weights. Random choices use a hash keyed on the element's `id` (if present) or its number, or on the piece key, so they are stable when upstream elements are added or removed.

Modes:

- **Random**: weighted random.
- **Cycle**: variants in turn (element k gets variant k mod N); with Use ID Attribute the id value replaces k.
- **By Attribute** (Map Attribute): the variant is looked up from `input_attribute` according to Map Pieces From.
- **Patches**: points in the same Worley noise cell share a variant, chosen by weight.
- **Noise**: the noise value, mapped to 0..1, is quantized through the cumulative weights, so variants form coherent clusters.
- **VEXpression**: each line of Rules is `piece names : expression`; the first line whose expression is non-zero decides.

Order is affected by Piece Filter, Shuffle and Offset, which matters for Cycle, Automatic ranges and the index output. Elements that match no rule get Unmatched Piece. Copy Attributes aggregates library attributes per piece (with the promotion method) and writes them onto the elements that picked that piece. The `report` output lists how many elements each variant received.

inputs.library: Optional geometry that defines the variants (and their weights). Without it the variants are the integers 0 to Count-1.

outputs.geo: Copy of `geo` with the variant attribute (and optional index and copied attributes).
outputs.report: Text summary with the number of elements per variant, and the unmatched count in rule-based modes.

params.group: Group pattern limiting which elements get a variant. Others keep their value.
params.attribute_class: Class on which the variant attribute is written.
params.piece_attribute: If set, elements sharing the same value of this attribute get the same variant (the piece is the unit that is assigned). Empty assigns per element.
params.mode: How variants are chosen; see the node description.
params.count: Number of variants (0 to Count-1) when no library is connected.
params.library_attribute: Attribute on the library (primitives, or points if there are no primitives) whose distinct values are the variants. Used only with a library.
params.piece_filter: Space-separated variant names to keep; empty keeps all. It is an error if nothing matches.
params.copy_attributes: Library attributes to copy onto elements, per piece (wildcards allowed). Requires a library. Piece values are combined with the Promotion Method; primitive attributes are read first, then point attributes of the piece's points.
params.allow_p: Allow `P` to be matched by Copy Attributes.
params.promotion: How the values of a piece are combined for Copy Attributes. String attributes support only max, min, mode, median, first and last.
params.output: Name of the variant attribute. A string attribute if the library values are strings, otherwise an integer.
params.index_output: Optional name of an integer attribute that receives the variant's index in the (filtered and ordered) list. Empty writes nothing.
params.shuffle: Randomly reorder the variants using the seed.
params.rand_seed: Seed for random choices, shuffle, Patches and Noise.
params.offset: Rotate the variant order by this many places.
params.id_attribute: Numeric attribute used instead of the element number by Cycle when Use ID Attribute is on.
params.use_id_attribute: Make Cycle use `id_attribute` values instead of the element number.
params.location_attribute: Position attribute sampled for Patches and Noise. For pieces, the piece's mean position is used.
params.element_size: Cell or noise feature size for Patches and Noise.
params.element_scale_x: Per-axis scale multiplied with the element size.
params.noise_offset_x: Offset subtracted from the position before dividing by the size.
params.max_octaves: Octaves for Noise mode. Above 1 uses standard fractal summation with lacunarity 2.
params.roughness: Amplitude falloff per octave for Noise mode.
params.weight_method: Where weights come from. Auto reads the library's weight attribute (first occurrence of each variant) or, without a library, the Weights text. Uniform gives equal weights. Piece Weights uses the Weights text. Weight Attribute averages the weight attribute over all primitives of each variant (library required).
params.weights: Weights typed as numbers in variant order (`3 1 1 1`), or as `name:weight` pairs for Piece Weights, where unlisted pieces get weight 0.
params.weight_attribute: Attribute on the library giving weights. Used with a library.
params.input_attribute: Attribute read by By Attribute mode: a 0..1 scalar for Weighted Unit, any numeric scalar for Automatic and Explicit, a string attribute for String. Pieces average their element values.
params.map_from: How By Attribute maps values to variants. Weighted Unit looks up the 0..1 value in the cumulative weights; Automatic splits the value range into equal parts, one per variant, ignoring weights; Explicit and String use Rules.
params.rules: Rules for Explicit, String and VEXpression, one per line as `piece [piece ...] : condition`. The condition is `min max` for Explicit, a wildcard pattern list for String and a wrangle expression for VEXpression. With several piece names on a line, one is picked at random. Earlier lines win. Lines starting with `#` are ignored.
params.unmatched_piece: Variant assigned to elements that match no rule. Empty leaves them unassigned (empty string, or -1 for integers).
params.unmatched_group: Optional group that receives the elements that matched no rule.

tips: Feed a noise attribute to By Attribute with Weighted Unit to get clustered variants.
Use Piece Attribute to give a whole connected chunk the same variant.

PCG_AttribFromVolume.summary: Samples a dense volume at point positions or primitive centers and writes the value as an attribute.
PCG_AttribFromVolume.description:
Looks up the volume at each point position (or primitive center) and stores the result. Modes: **Trilinear** interpolates between voxels, **Nearest** takes the closest voxel, **Gradient** writes a 3-component gradient vector (on an SDF this points along the surface normal direction). Outside the volume bounds, Clamp uses the value at the nearest edge, Constant writes Outside Value, and Keep does not write the element.

The volume must be a dense volume primitive (use Convert to make `volume_sdf` or `volume_fog`). A newly created attribute has one component, or three for Gradient. The `report` output gives the volume resolution and how many elements were sampled or outside.

inputs.geo: Geometry whose points or primitives sample the volume.
inputs.volume: Geometry containing the dense volume primitive(s).

outputs.geo: Copy of `geo` with the sampled attribute.
outputs.report: Text summary: which volume, its resolution, number of sampled and outside elements.

params.group: Group pattern limiting which elements are sampled. Others keep their value.
params.attribute_class: Sample at point positions, or at primitive centers.
params.volume_select: Which volume to use: empty for the first, a number for the nth, or a name matched against the primitive `name` attribute.
params.attribute: Name of the attribute written. If it exists with a different component count it is replaced.
params.mode: Trilinear interpolates, Nearest takes the closest voxel, Gradient samples the central-difference gradient (vector).
params.outside: Behaviour for positions outside the volume: Clamp to the border value, write a constant, or keep the existing value (do not write).
params.outside_value: Value written for positions outside the volume when Outside is Constant.

PCG_AttribFromVolume.houdini_notes: Covers Attribute from Volume and Volume Sample.

PCG_AttribInterpolate.summary: Interpolates source geometry attributes onto points using the source primitive each point lies on.
PCG_AttribInterpolate.description:
Typically placed after Scatter or Ray: each point has `sourceprim` recording which primitive of `source` it belongs to. The node computes where the point lies in that primitive and interpolates the source attributes there.

By default the barycentric coordinates are **recovered from the point's position** within the primitive's triangles, which is exact for any polygon. A `(u, v)` pair is ambiguous for quads (the same pair is valid in both triangles of a quad), and scatter on quad meshes is the most common case; on such meshes a linear attribute interpolated via UV was off by up to 0.97 in tests while the position-based path was exact to about 1e-6. Turn on Use UV Attribute for Houdini's behaviour, where the UV attribute holds the coordinates and its third component selects the triangle inside the primitive.

Points whose `sourceprim` is out of range, or outside `group`, are unchanged.

inputs.geo: Geometry (points) that receives the interpolated attributes.
inputs.source: Geometry providing the attributes and the primitives.

outputs.geo: Copy of `geo` with the interpolated attributes.

params.group: Group pattern limiting which elements are written.
params.attribute_class: Class on `geo` that is written (points or vertices).
params.attributes: Names of attributes to interpolate, space separated, wildcards allowed (`*` for all).
params.prim_attribute: Integer attribute on `geo` giving the source primitive number for each element. It must exist.
params.uv_attribute: Attribute holding the primitive UV when Use UV Attribute is on. When off, coordinates come from the point position.
params.use_uv_attribute: Use the stored primitive UV (Houdini's method) instead of recovering barycentric coordinates from the position.

PCG_AttribMirror.summary: Copies point attributes from one side of a plane to the mirrored points on the other side.
PCG_AttribMirror.description:
Defines a mirror plane by origin and normal direction. Points on the Source Side keep their values (points exactly on the plane are not modified). For every point on the other side, the position is mirrored across the plane and the attribute value is fetched there: **Closest Point** takes the value of the nearest source-side point; **Surface** interpolates on the source-side triangles with barycentric weights (requires triangles with all corners on the source side).

Vector attributes listed in Vectors are reflected through the plane; quaternion attributes listed in Quaternions are mirrored as H*R*H, which stays a proper rotation. String attributes are copied from the nearest point. Only point attributes are handled. `P` is never copied. The `report` output lists the attributes, the number of mirrored points and the number rejected by Max Distance.

inputs.geo: Geometry whose point attributes are mirrored.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with mirrored attribute values on the destination side.
outputs.report: Text summary: attributes mirrored, number of mirrored points and number too far.

params.group: Point group pattern limiting which destination (other side) points are written.
params.attributes: Point attributes to mirror, space separated, wildcards allowed.
params.origin_x: A point on the mirror plane.
params.direction_x: Normal of the mirror plane. Normalized internally; must not be zero.
params.source_side: Which side of the plane supplies the values. Positive is the side the direction points to.
params.lookup: How the value at the mirrored position is found: nearest source point, or interpolation on the source surface.
params.tolerance: Distance from the plane within which a point counts as on the plane and is used as a source.
params.max_distance: Mirrored points whose lookup distance exceeds this are left unchanged. 0 means unlimited.
params.vectors: Attributes (patterns) treated as vectors and reflected through the plane, for example `N v up`.
params.quaternions: Attributes (patterns) treated as orientation quaternions and mirrored as H*R*H.

PCG_AttribNoise.summary: Adds noise to attributes such as position, color or any numeric attribute.
PCG_AttribNoise.description:
Noise is a pure function of position: lattice values come from a hash of integer cell coordinates, so the same world position always gives the same value regardless of point order or upstream edits, and two meshes meet seamlessly. Several noise bases and fractal modes are provided, with optional domain warping and a time axis for animation.

Processing order: sample position `(position + Offset + VEXpression) / Element Size`, optional warp, fractal noise in -1..1, Bias/Gain, Gamma, Contrast, remap ramp (all in 0..1 space so they stay valid when the amplitude changes), absolute and invert, mapping to the range, optional normalize to a target range over the selected elements, then the operation, clamping, unit length and blend. Elements outside `group` are unchanged.

With Noise Along Vector on, a single scalar noise is pushed along a direction attribute, typically `N`; a grid becomes a mountain. Fractal modes differ in where detail is added: Standard is evenly rough, while Terrain and Hybrid Terrain multiply octaves so high areas become rougher and valleys flatter.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the noisy attributes.

params.group: Group pattern restricting which elements are adjusted. Elements outside the group keep their values.
params.blend: Blend between the original (0) and the noisy result (1). Ignored when Blend Attribute is set.
params.blend_attribute: Optional attribute giving the blend per element (first component, clamped to 0..1); replaces the constant Blend.
params.attribute_type: Auto uses the existing component count (new attributes named like `P`, `N`, `Cd`, `v`, `up` or `scale` get 3, others 1). Float uses one noise value spread over all components. Vector creates a 3-component attribute with independent noise per component.
params.attribute_names: Attributes to add noise to, space separated, wildcards allowed. Names that do not exist yet are created.
params.use_x: Apply noise to the first component of 3-component attributes.
params.use_y: Apply noise to the second component of 3-component attributes.
params.use_z: Apply noise to the third component of 3-component attributes.
params.attribute_class: Attribute class that is modified.
params.noise_along_vector: Compute one scalar noise and push the attribute along a vector attribute instead of giving each component its own noise. With `N` this turns a grid into terrain.
params.vector_attribute: Vector attribute that gives the push direction (normalized). Must have 3 components; compute it with Normal if missing.
params.range_values: Value range of the noise before the operation. Zero Centered: -Amplitude to +Amplitude. Zero to One: 0 to Amplitude. One Centered: 1 +- Amplitude (for Multiply). Negative: -Amplitude to 0. Min/Max: from Min to Max. Min + Range Length: Min to Min + length. Middle +- Range Length: Middle - length to Middle + length.
params.operation: How the noise is combined with the existing value. Set Initial only writes when the attribute does not exist; Minimum and Maximum compare per component. For attributes that do not exist, Minimum and Maximum take the noise.
params.amplitude: Size of the noise for the Zero Centered, Zero to One, One Centered and Negative ranges.
params.min_value: Lower end of the range for Min/Max and Min + Range Length.
params.max_value: Upper end of the range for Min/Max.
params.middle_value: Centre of the range for Middle +- Range Length.
params.range_length: Length parameter for Min + Range Length (full length) and Middle +- Range Length (extends this far on each side of Middle).
params.use_remap_ramp: Reshape the noise with the remap ramp. Applied in the 0..1 noise space so it is independent of amplitude.
params.remap_ramp: Ramp mapping noise value (horizontal, 0..1) to a new value (vertical). Can create plateaus and cliffs. Written as `position:value` pairs.
params.use_value_correction: Apply Bias and Gain to the 0..1 noise value.
params.bias: Shifts the noise distribution toward lower or higher values (0.5 = no change).
