params.gain: Pushes values toward the middle or the extremes (0.5 = no change).
params.gamma: Gamma on the 0..1 noise value, `t^(1/gamma)`. Applied after Bias/Gain, skipped at 1.
params.contrast: Contrast around 0.5 on the 0..1 noise value. Applied after gamma, skipped at 1.
params.clamp_min: Lower limit when Use Clamp Min is on.
params.clamp_max: Upper limit when Use Clamp Max is on.
params.recompute_normals: After modifying, recompute normals if the geometry already has an `N` attribute.
params.post_absolute: Fold the noise with an absolute value, producing sharp ridges where it crosses zero.
params.post_invert: Negate the noise, turning valleys into ridges.
params.use_normalize: Stretch the noise of the selected elements exactly to the Normalize range.
params.normalize_min: Target range of normalization (first value = low end, second = high end).
params.noise_type: Noise basis. Value and Perlin are lattice noises, Simplex avoids axis-aligned artifacts, the Worley, Manhattan and Chebyshev types are distance-to-feature-point (cellular) noises with different metrics; the `*_f2f1` variants use second minus first nearest distance.
params.location_attribute: Position used to sample the noise (default `P`). Taken from the attribute class if present with 3 components, otherwise from the points (primitives use their center, detail the mean).
params.element_size_x: Feature size (wavelength) per axis. Larger values give larger patterns; different values per axis stretch the noise. The sample position is divided by this.
params.offset_x: Offset added to the sample position, to move the noise pattern.
params.rand_seed: Seed that selects a different noise pattern. Noise is a function of position, so identical positions always give identical values.
params.use_vexpression: Add the result of the expression to the sample offset.
params.vexpression: Wrangle expression returning a vector per element, added to the sample position. It must return a vector, for example `set(0, @P.y * 0.1, 0)`.
params.fractal: Octave combination. Standard (fBm) sums octaves evenly; Terrain multiplies octaves so peaks get rougher and valleys flatter; Hybrid Terrain multiplies with weights clamped to 1, giving sharp ridges and flat valleys.
params.octaves: Number of noise layers for fractal types other than None.
params.fractal_offset: Offset used by the Terrain and Hybrid Terrain types.
params.warp: Distance in world units by which the sample position is displaced by another noise before sampling. 0 disables warping, and the next two parameters then have no effect.
params.warp_element_size: Feature size of the warp noise.
params.use_animation: Add a time axis to the noise. The pattern evolves in place along this fourth dimension rather than sliding.
params.time_element_size: Feature size along the time axis; larger values make the evolution slower.

PCG_AttribNoise.houdini_notes: Covers Attribute Noise and Mountain (Noise Along Vector with `N`). In Middle +- Range Length the range extends Range Length to each side of Middle, which is different from the Attribute Adjust nodes where the length is the total width.

PCG_AttribPromote.summary: Moves attributes between point, vertex, primitive and detail classes, reducing values when several sources map to one target.
PCG_AttribPromote.description:
Works by first building a table of (source element, target element) pairs and then reducing each target's values with the chosen method. When expanding (for example point to vertex) each target has a single source, so the method has no effect; when reducing (vertex to point) it combines the values. This lets all class combinations share one code path.

If a piece attribute is given, values are reduced per piece instead of per target element: all target elements with the same piece value receive the same result. The piece attribute is read from the New Class and must be integer or string; it is ignored for detail targets.

`original_name` accepts name patterns (`uv*`, `* ^P`) to move several attributes at once. In the new name, `*` is replaced by the original attribute name, which allows batch renaming. Integer attributes stay integer and are rounded rather than truncated after averaging. String attributes can only use Mode, First Match and Last Match when values have to be combined.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with attributes on the new class.

params.original_name: Names of the attributes to promote, space separated, wildcards and exclusions allowed. It is an error if nothing matches.
params.original_class: Class the attributes currently live on.
params.piece_attribute: Integer or string attribute on the new class that defines pieces. Used when Piece Attribute is on.
params.use_piece: Reduce per piece (value of the piece attribute) instead of per target element.
params.method: How multiple source values are combined: average, maximum, minimum, sum, mode (most common value; ties give the smallest), median, sum of squares, root mean square, or the first or last value found.
params.new_name: Name of the promoted attribute. A `*` is replaced by the original name. Used when Change New Name is on; otherwise the original name is kept.
params.change_new_name: Give the promoted attribute a different name.
params.delete_original: Remove the original attribute after promotion (unless the class and name stay the same).

PCG_AttribPromote.houdini_notes: Houdini's Array of All Values and Array of Unique Values methods are not available, because attributes here are always fixed-size arrays and cannot hold variable-length arrays.

PCG_AttribRandomize.summary: Writes random values, directions or orientations into an attribute.
PCG_AttribRandomize.description:
Used after scattering to add variation to `pscale`, `orient`, color and so on. The random stream is keyed on an id attribute when given, so inserting, deleting or sorting upstream points does not reshuffle the existing values.

Three modes: **Value** fills each component independently from a distribution; **Direction** produces unit vectors on a sphere, in a cone, in a disc or along a line, optionally with random length; **Orientation** produces quaternions, either a fully random rotation or a rotation about an axis by a random angle.

Directions are not made by randomizing each component and normalizing, which would favour the corners of the cube. Sphere and cone directions are uniform in the cosine of the polar angle, and fully random orientations use Shoemake's method, so they are uniform over all rotations (random Euler angles would cluster near the poles).

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the randomized attribute.

params.group: Group pattern restricting which elements are adjusted. Elements outside the group keep their values.
params.attribute_class: Attribute class that holds the attribute.
params.name: Name of the attribute to write. It is created if it does not exist.
params.combine: How the random values merge with the existing ones. Multiply treats a missing attribute as 1 (not 0). Minimum and Maximum take the random value when the attribute is missing or has a different component count.
params.global_scale: Multiplier applied to the generated values before the operation. Not applied to orientations, since scaling a quaternion is not a rotation.
params.mode: Value generates numbers in each component; Direction generates unit vectors (optionally with random length); Orientation generates quaternions.
params.distribution: Distribution of Value mode. Uniform is between Min and Max; Gaussian uses Mean and Standard Deviation; Power raises the uniform value to the exponent first (an exponent above 1 gives many small values and a few large ones); Constant writes Min; Two Values picks Max with the given probability and Min otherwise; Uniform Discrete steps from Min to Max by Step Size, both ends included; Exponential, Log-Normal and Cauchy are centred on Mean as the median; Custom Discrete picks from the value list; Inside Sphere is uniform inside the unit sphere (circle or ball depending on dimensions).
params.dimensions: Number of components generated in Value mode (1 to 4).
params.min_x: Lower end of the range per component. For Constant it is the value; for Two Values it is Value A.
params.max_x: Upper end of the range per component. For Two Values it is Value B.
params.mean: Mean for Gaussian. For Exponential, Log-Normal and Cauchy it is the median. Log-Normal needs a positive value.
params.stddev: Standard deviation for Gaussian; spread in log space for Log-Normal; scale (gamma) for Cauchy.
params.prob_b: Probability (0..1) of choosing Max (Value B) for Two Values.
params.value_list: Values for Custom Discrete, one group per line (`min-max:step` expands to a series); append `w=weight` for the group's probability.
params.shape: Direction mode: Sphere is uniform on the sphere, Cone is inside a cone around the axis, Disc is perpendicular to the axis, Line is along the axis in either sense. Orientation mode: Sphere is a fully random rotation (uniform over all rotations); the others rotate randomly about the axis.
params.axis_x: Reference axis for the Cone, Disc and Line shapes and for rotations in Orientation mode.
params.cone_angle: Half-angle of the cone in degrees (Cone shape).
params.angle_min: Range of rotation angle about the axis in degrees, for Orientation mode with shapes other than Sphere (first value = minimum, second = maximum).
params.length_min: Range of the vector length for Direction mode (first = minimum, second = maximum). Equal values give unit vectors.
params.id_attribute: Optional numeric attribute whose first component is the random key instead of the element number. Results then do not change when upstream elements are added, removed or reordered.

PCG_AttribRandomize.houdini_notes: Houdini's Constant, Two Values, Uniform (Discrete), Exponential, Log-Normal, Cauchy, Custom Discrete and Inside Sphere distributions reuse the Min, Max, Mean and Standard Deviation fields as described on the parameters.

PCG_AttribRename.summary: Renames attributes or groups using old:new pairs, with wildcard support.
PCG_AttribRename.description: Each pair is written `old:new` (an `=` also works) and pairs are separated by spaces. A wildcard in the old name carries the matched part over to the `*` in the new name: `uv*:tex*` renames `uv1` to `tex1` and `uvSet` to `texSet`. Renaming a name that does not exist is an error that lists the available names. With Rename Groups on, group names are renamed instead of attributes (groups do not exist on the detail class).

inputs.geo: Geometry with attributes or groups to rename.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the renamed attributes or groups.

params.attribute_class: Class whose attributes (or groups) are renamed.
params.rename: Rename pairs `old:new` separated by spaces. A `*` in the old name matches any text and is substituted into the new name.
params.rename_groups: Rename groups of the chosen class rather than attributes.

PCG_AttribRename.houdini_notes: Covers Attribute Rename and Group Rename in one node.

PCG_AttribReorient.summary: Rotates vector and quaternion point attributes to follow a deformation between a rest and a deformed pose.
PCG_AttribReorient.description:
After a deformation, attributes such as `N`, `up`, `v` and `orient` still describe the undeformed shape. For each point the node estimates a local rotation from the one-ring neighbourhood of the point in the rest and deformed positions (Kabsch fit). Vector attributes (3 components) are rotated by it and orientation quaternions (4 components) are rotated by left multiplication. On a collinear neighbourhood (curves, end points) the roll about the tangent is undetermined, so the minimum rotation between the two tangents is used.

The attributes are read from the deformed geometry, or from the rest geometry if missing there. Both inputs must have the same point count. Other component counts and string attributes are skipped; `P` is never modified. The `report` output lists the processed attributes.

inputs.geo: Deformed geometry. It receives the reoriented attributes.
inputs.rest: Geometry in the rest pose, with the same points and connectivity.

outputs.geo: Copy of the deformed geometry with rotated attributes.
outputs.report: Text summary of the attributes that were reoriented.

params.attributes: Point attributes to reorient, space separated, wildcards allowed. Vectors rotate by the local rotation; quaternions are multiplied by it.

PCG_AttribStringEdit.summary: Finds and replaces text inside string attributes using substring, wildcard or regular-expression matching.
PCG_AttribStringEdit.description: Edits the values of one or more string attributes (names separated by spaces, wildcards allowed). Modes: **Substring** replaces every occurrence of Find; **Wildcard** matches the whole string against a pattern containing `*`, and what each `*` captured is placed in order into the `*` of Replace (`piece*_old` with `chunk*` turns `piece12_old` into `chunk12`); **Regex** uses regular-expression substitution, where `\1` refers to groups. Values that do not match stay as they are. Only distinct values are processed, so large geometry with few names is fast. The `report` output summarizes the edits.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with edited strings.
outputs.report: Text summary of what was changed.

params.group: Group pattern limiting which elements are edited.
params.attribute_class: Class of the string attributes.
params.attributes: String attribute names to edit, space separated, wildcards allowed.
params.mode: How Find is interpreted: literal substring, whole-string wildcard pattern, or regular expression.
params.case_sensitive: Match upper and lower case as different characters.
params.find: Text, pattern or regular expression to look for.
params.replace: Replacement text. In Wildcard mode `*` receives the text captured by the corresponding `*` in Find; in Regex mode `\1` refers to capture groups.

PCG_AttribTransfer.summary: Transfers attributes and groups from a source geometry to a destination by spatial proximity.
PCG_AttribTransfer.description:
For each destination point, source points within `distance_threshold` are collected (the nearest `max_sample_count` of them, optionally only those with a matching `match_attribute` value). Their attribute values are averaged with the chosen kernel to give a **target value**. How much of that target replaces the original value is a separate quantity: an alpha derived from the distance of the *nearest* source point, which is 1 inside the threshold and falls to 0 over the last `blend_width` of distance. The result is `lerp(original, target, alpha)`. With Blend Width 0 this is a hard switch: reachable points are fully replaced, others untouched.

The two are separate so that smoothing (number of samples and kernel) and softness of the influence edge (blend width) can be tuned independently. Primitive attributes are matched by primitive centers. String attributes and groups cannot be averaged, so they take the value from the nearest source element (strings are left alone when alpha is below 0.5). `P` is not transferred. Detail attributes are copied as they are.

outputs.geo: Copy of `dest` with the transferred attributes and groups.

params.source_group: Point group pattern restricting which source points are used.
params.dest_group: Point group pattern restricting which destination points receive values. Primitive transfers consider only primitives whose points all lie in the group.
params.prim_attributes: Primitive attribute name patterns to transfer. Empty transfers none.
params.point_attributes: Point attribute name patterns to transfer (wildcards and `^` exclusions allowed). `P` is always skipped.
params.detail_attributes: Detail attribute name patterns to copy. Empty copies none.
params.point_groups: Point group names (patterns) to transfer, taken from the nearest source point.
params.prim_groups: Primitive group names (patterns) to transfer, taken from the nearest source primitive.
params.distance_threshold: Maximum distance within which source elements are considered. Also the radius for the kernel weights. Must be above 0.
params.blend_width: Width of the soft edge at the end of the threshold, in distance units. 0 gives a hard switch.
params.max_sample_count: Number of nearest source elements that are averaged. 1 takes the single nearest, which can look blocky; more samples give a smoother result.
params.kernel: Weights used when averaging samples. Uniform weights all equally; Inverse Distance favors close ones; Tent falls linearly with distance to the threshold; Gaussian and Smooth fall off smoothly to zero at the threshold.
params.match_attribute: Optional attribute (same class on both sides). Only source elements whose value equals the destination element's value are considered.

PCG_AttribTransfer.houdini_notes: Covers Attribute Transfer and Group Transfer. Vertex attributes are not transferred.

PCG_AttribTransferByUV.summary: Transfers attributes between geometries by matching UV coordinates instead of positions.
PCG_AttribTransferByUV.description:
For each destination point or vertex the node finds the source UV triangle that contains its UV and interpolates the source attribute with the barycentric coordinates there. The two geometries may differ in topology and position as long as their UV layouts match: baked high-resolution colors can be moved to a low-resolution mesh, and transferring `P` wraps one geometry onto another via UV space.

Sources can be point, vertex or primitive attributes; strings take the value of the dominant corner. A transferred `N` is renormalized. Where a destination UV lies outside every UV island, Nearest uses the closest UV triangle (limited by Max Distance) and Keep leaves the element untouched. The `report` output includes the number of queries inside UV islands, resolved to the nearest triangle, missed, and falling into overlapping UV regions.

inputs.source: Source geometry with matching UV layout and the attributes to transfer.

outputs.geo: Copy of the destination with the transferred attributes.
outputs.report: Text summary with counts of inside, nearest, missed and overlapping queries.

params.group: Point group pattern limiting which destination points are written (applies to the Point class only).
params.attribute_class: Destination class that is written: points or vertices.
params.attributes: Source attribute names to transfer, space separated, wildcards allowed. The UV attribute itself is excluded. Including `P` transfers positions.
params.uv_attribute: Name of the UV attribute on the destination (vertex or point attribute with at least two components).
params.source_uv: Name of the UV attribute on the source. Empty uses the same name as the destination.
params.outside: Behaviour for destination UVs outside all source UV islands: use the nearest source triangle, or leave the element unchanged.
params.max_distance: Largest allowed distance in UV space for the Nearest fallback. 0 means unlimited.

PCG_AttribTransformExtract.summary: Computes one rigid transform per piece between a rest and an animated copy of the same geometry.
PCG_AttribTransformExtract.description:
Both inputs must have identical topology. Points are grouped into pieces by the `name` style attribute (primitive attribute first, otherwise point attribute), and for each piece a rigid fit (rotation plus translation, no scaling) from rest to animated points is computed. Pieces with fewer than 3 points use translation only.

Two point clouds are produced, one point per piece: `template` has the piece center moved by the transform plus an `orient` quaternion, and `rest_points` has the rest piece center with an identity `orient`. Plug them into the template and rest inputs of Transform Pieces to make another geometry (for example high-resolution debris) follow each piece exactly. The piece key is copied onto both outputs. The `report` output gives the number of pieces and the largest fit error (RMS).

inputs.animated: Same geometry in the animated pose (same point count and topology).

outputs.template: One point per piece at the animated position, with an `orient` quaternion for the piece rotation.
outputs.rest_points: One point per piece at the rest center, with an identity `orient`.
outputs.report: Text summary with the piece count and the largest rigid-fit RMS error.

params.piece_attribute: Attribute on `rest` (primitive attribute, or else point attribute) that identifies the piece each element belongs to.

PCG_AttribTransformExtract.houdini_notes: Piece-wise version of Extract Transform. For decomposing matrix attributes use Attribute Transform Extract (Houdini).

PCG_AttribTransformExtractHou.summary: Decomposes 9- or 16-component matrix point attributes into translate, rotate and scale/shear/stretch attributes.
PCG_AttribTransformExtractHou.description:
Splits matrix attributes (9 components = 3x3, 16 components = 4x4 with translation in the last row; same convention as Transform by Attribute) into separate attributes. Two decompositions are offered. **Polar** writes rotation as Euler angles (degrees) plus a symmetric `stretch` 3x3 matrix, with `H3 = Stretch * R`. **Crack** writes rotation, scale and shear, and is the inverse of what the Transform SOP builds for the chosen transform order. Translation is written only for 16-component matrices.

A rotation matrix has several equivalent Euler angle triples. The Euler filter picks, per point, the solution closest to a reference angle: the already filtered angle of its parent in the chosen hierarchy, or the Hint for points without a parent. Points outside `group` receive defaults (translation 0, rotation 0, scale 1, shear 0, identity stretch). If no attribute matches, the geometry passes through and the `report` explains why.

Output names are built as `prefix + matrix name + suffix`.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the decomposed attributes.
outputs.report: Text summary: matrices processed, attributes written, point and root counts.

params.group: Point group pattern limiting which points are decomposed.
params.hierarchy: Where parent points for the Euler filter come from. None filters against the Hint only; Topology uses the previous point along each primitive; Pieces / Points uses the previous selected point with the same piece attribute value.
params.piece_attribute: Integer or string point attribute defining pieces for Pieces / Points. If missing or float, all points form one piece.
params.hint_x: Reference Euler angles (degrees) used for points without a parent.
params.decomposition: Polar writes Euler rotation and a stretch matrix; Crack writes rotation, scale and shear using the transform order.
params.xform_order: Transform order assumed by Crack (for example SRT: scale, then rotate, then translate).
params.rotate_order: Rotation order of the output Euler angles.
params.attributes: Matrix attributes to decompose, space separated, wildcards allowed. Only point attributes with 9 or 16 components are considered.
params.t_prefix: Prefix of the translation attribute name (16-component matrices only).
params.t_suffix: Suffix of the translation attribute name.
params.r_prefix: Prefix of the rotation attribute name.
params.r_suffix: Suffix of the rotation attribute name.
params.stretch_prefix: Prefix of the stretch matrix attribute name (Polar).
params.stretch_suffix: Suffix of the stretch matrix attribute name (Polar).
params.s_prefix: Prefix of the scale attribute name (Crack).
params.s_suffix: Suffix of the scale attribute name (Crack).
params.sh_prefix: Prefix of the shear attribute name (Crack).
params.sh_suffix: Suffix of the shear attribute name (Crack).

PCG_AttribTransformExtractHou.houdini_notes: Matrices are read in Houdini's convention (row vectors, translation in the fourth row of 16-component attributes), the same as everywhere else in the plugin. The rest/animated rigid fit per piece is the separate Attribute Transform Extract node.

PCG_ClusterPoints.summary: Groups points into clusters with k-means and writes a cluster index, cluster centers and optional averaged points or boxes.
PCG_ClusterPoints.description:
Runs k-means on the chosen attribute (default `P`, but color or any numeric attribute works) with k-means++ initialization; a fixed seed reproduces the result. Each point receives an integer cluster number in the attribute named `name`; if a cluster loses all its points the farthest point becomes its new center. Additional control attributes can be added to the feature vector, each multiplied by its own weight.

The main output is chosen by Output: the original points with the cluster attribute, one averaged point per cluster (position = mean, `size_attribute` = bounding box size including padding), both merged (in groups `clusterpoints` and `averagepoints`), or one bounding box per cluster. Cluster Filter keeps only listed clusters. The second output is always a point cloud of cluster centers with `cluster` and `count` attributes.

With Build Clusters off, no k-means is run: the existing integer attribute `name` defines the clusters. Points outside `group` get cluster -1 (or keep their previous value).

outputs.geo: Main result according to Output.
outputs.centroids: One point per cluster at the mean position, with `cluster` and `count` attributes.
outputs.report: Text summary: number of clusters, k-means iterations and total squared error.

params.group: Point group pattern limiting which points are clustered.
params.name: Name of the integer point attribute that receives the cluster number (also used as the existing attribute when Build Clusters is off).
params.output: Cluster Points keeps the input points; Average Points gives one point per cluster; Both merges the two; Boxes creates a box per cluster.
params.color_output: Points keeps colors unchanged. The two colored options assign a random `Cd` per cluster (there is no particle system, so both behave the same).
params.cluster_filter: Clusters to keep, written like point numbers (`3 4`, `3-6`). Points outside the chosen clusters are removed from the output. Empty keeps all.
params.attribute: Numeric point attribute whose values are clustered.
params.weight: Multiplier for the main attribute in the feature vector.
params.control_attribute2: Optional second attribute added to the feature vector.
params.weight2: Multiplier for the second control attribute.
params.control_attribute3: Optional third attribute added to the feature vector.
params.weight3: Multiplier for the third control attribute.
params.build_clusters: Run k-means. When off, use the existing `name` attribute as the clustering.
params.clusters: Number of clusters (limited to the number of points).
params.rand_seed: Seed for the initial centers and random colors.
params.copy_point_attributes: Give averaged points the other point attributes of the cluster: numeric values averaged over the points nearest to the center, strings from the nearest point.
params.max_sample_count: Number of points nearest to the center used for copied attributes.
params.size_attribute: Name of the vector attribute holding the cluster bounding box size on averaged points. Empty writes none.
params.padding_min_x: Amount the cluster bounding box is extended on the minimum side of each axis (Average Points and Boxes).
params.padding_max_x: Amount the cluster bounding box is extended on the maximum side of each axis.

PCG_Color.summary: Sets colors with a constant, random values, per-attribute random colors, a ramp over a scalar attribute, or an HSV adjustment.
PCG_Color.description:
Writes a 3-component color attribute (default `Cd`) on selected elements; others keep their color (or white if the attribute is new).

- **Constant**: one color for all.
- **Random**: one random color per element, keyed on `id` if it exists or on the element number.
- **Random by Attribute**: the same attribute value gets the same color (for example color pieces by `name`).
- **Ramp by Attribute**: a scalar (or the length of a vector) attribute is normalized to 0..1 and looked up in the ramp. With Auto Range the range is the minimum and maximum over the selected elements.
- **Adjust**: modifies the existing colors in HSV (hue shift, saturation and value multipliers) and adds optional random variation; with an attribute set the variation is shared per piece.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the color attribute.

params.group: Group pattern limiting which elements are colored.
params.attribute_class: Class on which the color is written.
params.mode: How colors are produced; see the node description.
params.rand_seed: Seed for random colors and random variation.
params.attribute: Attribute used by Random by Attribute (key), Ramp by Attribute (scalar value) and Adjust (piece key for shared random variation).
params.auto_range: Ramp by Attribute: use the minimum and maximum of the selected elements as the input range. When off, In Min and In Max are used.
params.in_min: Manual input range for Ramp by Attribute (first value = minimum, second = maximum).
params.ramp: Color ramp for Ramp by Attribute as `position:r,g,b` entries separated by spaces.
params.hue_shift: Adjust mode: hue rotation in degrees.
params.random_hue: Adjust mode: random hue variation, up to plus or minus this many degrees.
params.random_saturation: Adjust mode: random saturation variation as a fraction of the saturation (0.2 = plus or minus 20 percent).
params.random_value: Adjust mode: random value variation as a fraction.
params.name: Name of the color attribute written.

PCG_Color.houdini_notes: Combines the Color SOP with the HSV-adjust behaviour of Attribute Adjust Color. For the full Houdini Attribute Adjust Color semantics use Attribute Adjust Color.

PCG_EdgeTransport.summary: Propagates or accumulates a point attribute along a tree grown from root points over the edges.
PCG_EdgeTransport.description:
First a tree is built: **Network** runs shortest paths (edge length) from root points over all edges, each point attaching to its nearest root; **Curves** walks each polyline from its start (or from the end that lies in the root group); **Parent Attribute** takes parents from an integer point attribute. Then the Operation runs along the tree. Points that cannot be reached get value 0 and join the unreached group. The root of each point is written to the integer point attribute `transport_root`.

The first four operations are plain: **Distance** is the path length from the root, **Copy** passes the root value down, **Sum** adds the attribute along the path (including both ends), **Average** is the sum divided by the number of points on the path. The remaining ones follow Houdini: **Transport** takes the parent's value (root: zero or hold), **Transport from Root** uses the root's accumulated flow, **Total** sums ancestors' values without the point itself (root = 0), **Maximum** and **Minimum** take the extreme over the point and its ancestors. Integrate a Constant Value with Scale by Edge Length gives the distance along edges. Direction Backward goes from tips to roots and merges several children with the merge method. The `report` output gives reached, unreached and root counts.

inputs.geo: Geometry with edges (polylines or meshes) and points to transport on.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the result attribute, `transport_root` and the unreached group.
outputs.report: Text summary of reached, unreached and root counts.

params.method: How the tree is built: shortest paths over the edge network, along curves, or from a parent attribute.
params.curve_group: Primitive group pattern limiting which curves are walked (Curves method). Empty uses all.
params.point_group: Point group pattern limiting which points can take part (Network and Parent Attribute). Empty uses all.
params.attribute: Numeric point attribute to transport. Not needed for Distance.
params.direction: Forward goes from the roots toward the leaves; Backward goes from the leaves to the roots. Applies to the Houdini-style operations.
params.parent_attribute: Integer point attribute holding each point's parent point number (Parent Attribute method). Invalid or self references make the point a root.
params.root_choice: Network method: start from points in the root group, or from the first or last point (when unreached points remain, the lowest or highest remaining point becomes a new root).
params.root_group: Point group pattern for the roots. Network with Root Choice = Group requires it; for Curves it picks the end where each curve starts.
params.operation: What is computed along the tree; see the node description. Distance, Copy, Sum and Average are the basic set; the rest follow Houdini.
params.normalization: Per Component normalizes every connected tree separately to 0..1, Global normalizes everything together. Used when Use Normalization is on.
params.use_normalization: Normalize the result to 0..1 per component of the output.
params.new_root_value: Value at root points for Transport operations: zero, or hold the root's own attribute value.
params.integrate_constant: For Total: use 1 for every point instead of the attribute.
params.scale_by_edge_length: For the Houdini-style operations: multiply each step by the length of the edge to the parent.
params.split_method: Forward direction when a point has several children: Copy gives each child the full value, Split divides it evenly.
params.merge_method: Backward direction when several children meet at a parent: add, or take the maximum or minimum.
params.output: Name of the output attribute. Empty writes back into `attribute` (or into `transport` for Distance).
params.unreached_group: Name of the point group that receives unreachable points. Empty creates no group.

PCG_EdgeTransport.houdini_notes: The first four operations (Distance, Copy, Sum, Average) are this plugin's own and differ from Houdini: Sum includes the point itself, whereas Houdini's Total excludes it and sets the root to 0. Transport, Transport from Root, Total, Maximum and Minimum follow Houdini.

PCG_Enumerate.summary: Writes sequence numbers to elements or pieces, as integers or formatted names.
PCG_Enumerate.description: In **Elements** mode every selected element gets its index; with a piece attribute, numbering restarts in every piece. In **Pieces** mode every element gets the index of the piece it belongs to. The value is `Start + Step * index`. If Format is set (for example `piece_%d` or `%03d`) the value is written as a string, which is how the Name SOP is used; the format must contain exactly one integer placeholder. Pieces are ordered by first appearance or by sorted value. Elements outside `group` keep their value.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the numbering attribute.

params.group: Group pattern limiting which elements are numbered.
params.attribute_class: Class that is numbered.
params.mode: Elements numbers each element (restarting per piece if a piece attribute is set); Pieces gives every element its piece number.
params.piece_attribute: Attribute whose distinct values define pieces. Empty means no pieces (Pieces mode then treats everything as one piece).
params.order: How pieces are numbered: by first appearance in the geometry, or by sorted attribute value.
params.name: Name of the attribute written.
params.format: Optional format string with one integer placeholder such as `piece_%d` or `%03d`. If set, a string attribute is written. Empty writes integers.

PCG_Enumerate.houdini_notes: Covers Enumerate and the Name SOP (string format).

PCG_ExtractCentroid.summary: Reduces each piece of geometry to a single point at its centroid.
PCG_ExtractCentroid.description:
Splits the geometry into pieces (by attribute value, per primitive, per point, per connected component, or the whole geometry as one piece, using the same splitting as the For-Each loop) and computes a centroid per piece.

Center of Mass is **area weighted** (signed, using the face normal so concave faces cancel correctly) instead of averaging points, which would be biased toward finely tessellated areas: a box with one face subdivided 100 times and five single quads would otherwise shift toward the dense face. Bounding Box uses the center of the bounding box and Average Position the plain mean of the piece's points. Without faces, Center of Mass falls back to the point average.

Output as Points makes a new point cloud with one point per piece, carrying the piece value (the piece attribute, `sourceprim`, `sourcepoint` or `class`) and optionally attributes and groups transferred from the first element of each piece. Output as Attribute keeps the geometry and writes the centroid onto the pieces' own elements.

outputs.geo: Point cloud with one point per piece, or the input with a centroid attribute.

params.group: Group pattern limiting which elements take part.
params.run_over: How the geometry is split: by value of the piece attribute, per primitive, per point, by connected component, or as a single piece.
params.piece_attribute: Attribute defining pieces for Pieces mode (scalar or string).
params.piece_elements: Whether Pieces mode reads the piece attribute from primitives or from points.
params.method: How the centroid is computed: area-weighted center of mass, center of the bounding box, or average of the points.
params.output: Points creates a new point per piece; Attribute writes the centroid to an attribute on the original elements.
params.attribute_name: Name of the vector attribute for Attribute output.
params.use_attrib_out: Write the centroid attribute for Attribute output. When off, the geometry passes through unchanged.
params.use_transfer: Enable transferring attributes and groups to the output points.
params.transfer_attributes: Attribute name patterns copied from each piece's first element onto its output point (Points output).
params.transfer_groups: Group name patterns transferred in the same way.

PCG_ExtractCentroid.houdini_notes: Center of Mass is always the area centroid of the surface. Houdini computes the volume centroid for closed pieces; the two coincide for symmetric shapes but differ for asymmetric solid pieces.

PCG_Measure.summary: Measures area, perimeter, volume or curvature of primitives or points and optionally visualizes the result as color.
PCG_Measure.description:
Writes the measured value as a float attribute (default name `area`, `perimeter`, `volume` or `curvature` according to the measurement). Area uses the Newell area vector, not a triangle fan with absolute values, which would double count folded parts of concave polygons. Volume uses the same formula with a cone from an arbitrary point, `V = 1/3 (area vector . v0)`, so the sum over a closed mesh equals the enclosed volume regardless of the reference point. Curvature is the mean curvature from the cotangent Laplacian, signed by the point normal; Gaussian curvature is the angle defect divided by area (flat areas 0, a sphere of radius r gives 1/r^2). Primitive curvature is the average over its corners.

Elements outside `group` get 0. With Accumulate = Total every element in the group receives the total instead of its own value.

When a color attribute name is given, values are mapped through a color ramp over the Visualized Range. By default this range is the **median plus or minus half of Width times the MAD** (median absolute deviation) rather than min/max, because a single degenerate element would otherwise squash the ramp to a single color; most elements then show contrast and outliers saturate at the ends, which is what you look for. Bake Range writes the normalized 0..1 value (scaled to the remap range) into the output attribute instead of the raw measurement.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the measurement attribute, and optionally color, total and range group.

params.group: Group pattern limiting which elements are measured. Others get 0.
params.element_type: Measure primitives or points. Perimeter and Volume apply only to primitives.
params.measurement: Quantity to measure. For points, area is the area associated with the point.
params.accumulate: Per Element writes each element's own value; Total writes the sum over the group to all of its elements.
params.position_attribute: Point attribute to use as position instead of `P` (it must have 3 components).
params.color_attribute: Name of the attribute to receive the visualization color. Empty creates no color and the other Visualized Range options have no effect.
params.min_value: Lower end of the visualized range when Use Min is on.
params.use_min: Override the lower end of the visualized range with Min.
params.max_value: Upper end of the visualized range when Use Max is on.
params.use_max: Override the upper end of the visualized range with Max.
params.width: Size of the automatic range in units of the width measure (the range is center +- width/2 times the spread).
params.use_width: Compute the range from center and width. When off, the range is the minimum and maximum of the values.
params.width_mode: Spread measure used by Width: MAD (robust to outliers), standard deviation, or absolute (spread of 1).
params.center: Center of the automatic range: median, mean or zero.
params.color_ramp: Color scheme for the visualization. Custom uses the custom ramp text.
params.custom_ramp: Custom color ramp as `position:r,g,b` entries separated by spaces. Used when Color Ramp is Custom.
params.attribute_name: Name of the output attribute. Empty uses the default name of the measurement.
params.total_attribute: Optional name of a detail attribute that receives the total over the group.
params.range_group: Optional name of a group that receives the elements whose value lies inside the visualized range.
params.bake_range: Write the value normalized to the visualized range, scaled to the remap range, into the output attribute instead of the raw measurement.
params.remap_min: Output range of the baked values (first value = value at the low end of the visualized range, second = at the high end).

PCG_Name.summary: Writes a string attribute (default `name`) based on group membership, with an optional text replacement.
PCG_Name.description:
Two ways to assign names. With the default, Namings has one rule per line: `group : name`. The group can be a group name, wildcard, number list or expression, as in any group field; an empty group means all elements. Rules run in order and later rules overwrite earlier ones where groups overlap. Lines starting with `#` are disabled. With Name from Group on, every element is named after the group it belongs to (matching Group Mask); an element in several groups takes the last one in alphabetical order.

Afterwards a From to To substring replacement is applied to the whole attribute, replacing every occurrence or only the first. Unnamed elements keep their previous value (empty if the attribute is new). An existing numeric attribute with that name is replaced by a string attribute, noted in the `report`.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the string attribute.
outputs.report: Text summary: rules or groups used and number of elements named.

params.attribute: Name of the string attribute to write.
params.cls: Class on which the attribute is written.
params.name_from_group: Name elements after the groups they belong to instead of using Namings.
params.group_mask: Group name pattern selecting which groups are used when Name from Group is on.
params.namings: One rule per line, `group : name`. Later rules overwrite earlier ones. Lines starting with `#` are disabled.
params.global_replace: Replace every occurrence of From; when off only the first occurrence in each value is replaced.
params.from_: Text to search for in the resulting values (plain substring, no wildcards). Empty skips the replacement.

PCG_Name.houdini_notes: The numbered `piece_%d` style naming is done by Enumerate with its Format option.

PCG_Normal.summary: Computes normals on points, vertices, primitives or the detail, with smoothing control.
PCG_Normal.description:
**Point** normals are smooth with one normal per point, so there can be no hard edges. **Vertex** normals have one normal per corner and are grouped by Cusp Angle, which is the only way to represent hard edges: a corner only accumulates neighbouring faces that deviate from its own face by less than the cusp angle (a cube at 60 degrees keeps all edges hard, a sphere stays smooth). **Primitive** normals are one per face, meant for copy and align computations rather than shading. **Detail** gives one normal for the whole geometry, the normalized sum of area normals.

Weighting decides how the face normals around a point or corner are averaged. Normals are written to the attribute named by Normal Name. With Compute Normals off, the node does not compute anything and only post-processes existing normals (Make Unit Length, Reverse).

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the normal attribute.

params.group: Group pattern limiting which elements are computed.
params.group_type: How the group is interpreted. Guess reads it as a group of the class chosen in Add Normals to. A specific type reads the group in that class and expands it to the target class (touching elements count, for example a primitive group selects its points).
params.normal_name: Name of the attribute the normals are written to. Empty means `N`.
params.compute_normals: Compute new normals. When off, only Make Unit Length and Reverse are applied to the existing attribute.
params.add_to: Class that receives the normals. Detail ignores the group.
params.cusp_angle: Vertex normals only: maximum angle in degrees between faces whose normals are merged at a corner.
params.weighting: How surrounding face normals are averaged: by face area, equally per corner, or by the corner angle of each face (a large and a thin triangle then count by their opening angle at the point).
params.keep_zero: Where the computed normal is a zero vector (isolated points, degenerate faces) keep the previous value instead.
params.make_unit: Normalize existing normals in the group. Only takes effect when Compute Normals is off, since computed normals are already unit length.
params.reverse: Flip the normals in the group (done last).

PCG_OrientAlongCurve.summary: Writes a rotation-minimizing frame (tangent, up and orientation quaternion) on the points of curves.
PCG_OrientAlongCurve.description:
Builds a frame on every curve point by carrying the frame along the curve with the double reflection method, so it only twists where it must and does not flip at bends. It writes `N` (tangent, the +Z of Copy to Points), `up` (+Y) and `orient` (quaternion of the same frame, which Copy to Points prefers over `N` and `up`). Optional outputs are `side` (the X axis) and a curve-parameter attribute (normalized arc length 0..1), both off by default; any name left empty is not written.

On closed curves the twist accumulated going around the loop is spread evenly over the arc length so that the start and end frames match. Roll and twists rotate `up` about the tangent: `roll + (full_twists * 360 + partial_twist) * u` degrees, where `u` is the normalized arc length. Points on several curves take the frame from the last curve processed. Points not on a curve are left as they are.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with frame attributes on the curve points.

params.group: Primitive group pattern limiting which curves are processed.
params.tangent_type: How the tangent at a point is derived from its edges: average of the incoming and outgoing edge, the previous edge, or the next edge.
params.reverse: Flip the tangent, so copies face toward the start of the curve.
params.up_mode: Minimal Rotation starts from the Up vector at the first point and carries the frame forward. Constant orients every point toward the Up vector. Attribute uses the point attribute named by Up Attribute.
params.up_x: Up vector used by Minimal Rotation (at the start) and Constant modes.
params.up_attribute: Three-component point attribute giving the up direction in Attribute mode.
params.roll: Extra rotation of the up vector about the tangent, in degrees, applied equally along the curve.
params.full_twists: Number of complete 360 degree twists added along the length of the curve.
params.partial_twist: Additional twist in degrees added along the length of the curve.
params.tangent_name: Name of the tangent attribute. Empty skips it.
params.up_name: Name of the up attribute. Empty skips it.
params.orient_name: Name of the orientation quaternion attribute. Empty skips it.
params.side_name: Name of the optional side (X axis) attribute. Empty skips it.

PCG_OrientAlongCurve.houdini_notes: For a local frame that follows only the nearby edges, use PolyFrame instead; its curve normal is the Frenet normal and can flip.

PCG_PointVelocity.summary: Computes point velocity (and optionally acceleration) from positions on neighbouring frames.
PCG_PointVelocity.description:
Finite differences between the current positions and those of the previous and/or next frame, with `dt = 1 / FPS`. **Backward** is `(P - P_prev) / dt`, **Forward** is `(P_next - P) / dt` and **Central** is `(P_next - P_prev) / (2 dt)`. Auto picks Central if both neighbouring frames are connected, otherwise whichever one is.

Points are matched to the other frames by point number or by an id attribute. Unmatched points get zero velocity and are added to the group `no_velocity`. If Compute Acceleration is on and both frames are connected, `accel = (P_next - 2P + P_prev) / dt^2` is written to the point attribute `accel`. The `report` output tells the method and the matched and unmatched counts.

inputs.geo: Current frame geometry; receives the velocity.
inputs.prev: Optional geometry of the previous frame.
inputs.next: Optional geometry of the next frame.

outputs.geo: Copy of the current geometry with the velocity attribute and the `no_velocity` group.
outputs.report: Text summary: method, matched and unmatched points.

params.method: Difference scheme. Backward needs `prev`, Forward needs `next`, Central needs both. Auto chooses from what is connected.
params.fps: Frame rate that sets the time step `1 / fps`. Must be above 0.
params.match: How points are paired between frames: by point number or by matching attribute values.
params.id_attribute: Attribute present on both frames used for pairing when Match is By Attribute.
params.compute_accel: Also write the `accel` attribute. Requires both `prev` and `next`.

PCG_PolyFrame.summary: Writes a local frame (N, tangentu, tangentv) on points or primitives.
PCG_PolyFrame.description:
Each point or primitive gets a frame derived only from its immediate surroundings. `tangentu` comes from the chosen Style, `N` is the normal, and `tangentv = N x tangentu`. Degenerate cases (zero area, zero length, no UV change) write a zero vector, not NaN.

Styles for primitives: **Two Edges** uses the first edge as tangentu and the cross product of first and last edge as normal; **First Edge** uses the first edge with the Newell normal; **Centroid** points from the face center to the first vertex. For points on faces the corresponding values come from the incident face, averaged where needed. **UV** takes the direction of increasing `u` (the same definition as the tangent space of normal maps); **Attribute Gradient** takes the direction of steepest increase of a scalar point attribute within the face.

On curve points, `N` is the Frenet principal normal (pointing to the inside of the bend, undefined on straight segments and flipping at inflections). For a frame to place objects along a curve without flips use Orient Along Curve.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the frame attributes.

params.group: Group pattern limiting which primitives take part.
params.entity: Write the frame on points or on primitives.
params.style: How tangentu is derived; see the node description.
params.uv_attribute: UV attribute for the UV style (vertex or point attribute).
params.gradient_attribute: Scalar point attribute for the Attribute Gradient style.
params.n_name: Name of the normal attribute. Empty skips it.
params.tangentu_name: Name of the tangentu attribute. Empty skips it.
params.tangentv_name: Name of the tangentv attribute. Empty skips it.

PCG_TangentField.summary: Computes the smoothest direction field with 1-, 2-, 4- or 6-fold symmetry on a surface.
PCG_TangentField.description:
Produces a field of unit tangent vectors on a polygon mesh that varies as little as possible from point to point. Symmetry sets the number of equivalent directions: 1 is an arrow, 2 a line, 4 a cross and 6 a snowflake; with symmetry above 1 each point stores one of the n equivalent directions. Neighbouring points are compared after parallel transport along the edge, and the field minimizing the total difference is found: a constrained linear solve when guides are present, otherwise the smallest eigenvector of the smoothness operator.

Guides come from a vector point attribute, or from the principal curvature directions (Align). Curvature alignment weighs by relative anisotropy, so isotropic regions such as spheres and planes get no imposed direction. Principal directions are lines (sign does not matter), so Align needs Symmetry of 2 or more. The smoothest field is found in a relaxed sense, which can leave pairs of cancelling singularities; guides or curvature alignment suppress them.

On closed surfaces singularities are unavoidable. The `report` output lists their count and the index sum (equal to `n * Euler characteristic`; on a sphere 2 for n = 1 and 8 for n = 4).

inputs.geo: Polygon mesh to compute the field on.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the tangent attribute.
outputs.report: Text summary with the guided point count, singularity count and index sum.

params.symmetry: Number of equivalent directions per point: 1 arrow, 2 line, 4 cross, 6 snowflake.
params.guide_attribute: Optional vector point attribute whose tangential component guides the field.
params.guide_weight: Strength of the guide relative to smoothness. Higher values follow the guide more closely.
params.align: Align the field with the maximum or minimum principal curvature direction (on a cylinder, around the circumference or along the axis). Needs Symmetry of 2 or more.
params.rand_seed: Seed for the starting vector of the eigenvector solver, which can change the field when several solutions are equally smooth.
params.output: Name of the point attribute that receives the field.

PCG_Wrangle.summary: Runs a short vectorized script over points, primitives, vertices or the detail, with VEX-style attribute syntax.
PCG_Wrangle.description:
The code is not executed once per element. It runs **once for the whole geometry**, with `@P` being an array of shape (N, 3), and the script is Python/numpy with the VEX-like attribute shorthand: `@Cd`, `@P.y`, `@ptnum`, `@numpt`, `@primnum`, `@numprim`. Component access `.x .y .z .w` can be read and written. Type prefixes `f@` `i@` `v@` `s@` `2@` `3@` `4@` `p@` declare the type, and a typed assignment converts the value to it as in VEX (`i@id = @P.x * 10` truncates to integers, `v@c = 0.5` fills three components). `@group_name` reads and writes the group `name` of the Run Over class. `rand(x)`, `ch("name")` (and `chv`, `chi`, `chs`) are available, as are `np` and `math`.

Because the script is vectorized, per-element branching is written with numpy masks and `np.where` rather than `if`. If a group is set, the code still runs on all elements and the unselected rows are restored afterwards, so errors such as division by zero can still occur in unselected elements. Attributes that do not exist are created from the assigned shape.

The optional `geo1`, `geo2` and `geo3` inputs give access to other geometries by index in functions such as `point(1, "P", i)`, `npoints(2)` or `getbbox_size(3)`; without an index, input 0 is used. `ch("name")` in the code creates a custom parameter `name` on the node (type from the function: `ch`/`chf` float, `chi` integer, `chv` vector, `chs` string); see [`ch()` parameters](../concepts/wrangle.md#ch-parameters). The complete syntax is on [Wrangle syntax](../concepts/wrangle.md).

inputs.geo1: Optional second geometry, input 1 in functions such as `point(1, ...)`.

outputs.geo: Copy of the input with the changes made by the code.

params.run_over: Class whose elements `@` attributes refer to. In primitive context `@P` is the primitive center and is read-only.
params.code: The script. Executed once over all elements with `@attribute` shorthand; see the node description.
params.group: Group pattern limiting which elements keep the result. Others are restored to their original values.
params.ch_params: Internal JSON text with the values of the node's custom parameters (vectors also per component), read with `ch()`. It is maintained by the frontend; do not edit by hand.

PCG_Wrangle.houdini_notes: Replaces Attribute Wrangle, Attribute Expression, Attribute Combine, Attribute Swap and Rest Position through code. Unlike VEX the code is vectorized instead of run per element, so `if` and `for` over elements are written with numpy masks.
